item.title: Giants’ Zvada Struggles Spark Debate Over Ben Sauls Options
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Rookie kicker Dominic Zvada is drawing sharp criticism from a loud group of New York Giants fans who want him off the roster. The pressure comes after a rough stretch where the young kicker missed six of his last 14 field-goal attempts. While the start of the season looked perfect with nine straight makes, the last four games have shown clear cracks in his game. Per Big Blue View , a vocal part of the fan base believes the team should have already booted Zvada to the curb. Head coach John Harbaugh pushed back against the idea of making a quick change during the week. “You can’t, as soon as a guy doesn’t make a play, start firing people left and right,” he said. He noted that finding a new player who is definitely better is much harder than just saying someone has to go. The Case for Keeping Zvada Blowing the whistle on Zvada right now might not fix the real problem. Per Big Blue View, the main issue is a much-discussed problem from the right hash mark that has cost the team points. Even with the misses, Zvada has proven he can hit the big shots that other kickers might dread. Why Ben Sauls Is Not the Answer Many fans point to left-footed Ben Sauls as the savior who could fix the kicking woes. Sauls was an elixir for the Giants at the end of the 2025 season, making all 15 of his kicks over a three-game span. His record included eight field goals and seven extra points, with a longest kick of 45 yards. However, the Giants cannot just call him up if he is not on the team. Big Blue View reports that Ben Sauls is not on a 53-man roster or practice squad at this time. There is also a question of whether Sauls can handle the long kicks Zvada attempts. While Sauls was great in the spring and summer, he had his own technique issues before the season started. During summer practice, he was not nearly as consistent as Zvada, having been terrible in the spring by consistently pushing kicks to the left. When the two kickers competed for the spot, deciding which of them should win the job was easily done. The Harbaugh Reality Check John Harbaugh knows that swapping players is easy in theory but hard in practice. The Giants do not have a ready-made replacement sitting on the bench who can hit 50-yarders with confidence. The Giants will face the Jacksonville Jaguars next on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:25 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium.

item.description: Nvidia's quarterly earnings call on Tuesday was its first with CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress at the helm alongside the company's first board chair, Harvey C. Jones. item.title: Devon Dampier wins multiple national weekly awards
item.description: Utah quarterback Devon Dampier scores a touchdown in front of Arizona safety Gavin Hunter (23) in the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Tucson, Ariz. | Rick Scuteri, Associated Press The awards are pouring in this week for Utah quarterback Devon Dampier after he led the No. 2 Utes to a 40-39 victory over No. 23 Arizona on Saturday night. Dampier accounted for 304 yards and four touchdowns and threw a 70-yard touchdown to Creed Whittemore for the win, which improved the Utes’ record to 10-0. The senior quarterback was named the Big 12’s co-offensive player of the week for the second consecutive time, but also received two national awards. Dampier was named the Maxwell Award Player of the Week and the Davey O’Brien National Quarterback of the Week. The Maxwell Award is given to the best all-around player in college football at the end of the season, while the Davey O’Brien Award is given to the nation’s best quarterback. Dampier has thrown for 2,257 yards and 22 touchdowns and rushed for 582 yards and nine scores this season. He has been one of the best quarterbacks in all of college football this year and currently has the third-best odds to win the Heisman Trophy. Utah Utes quarterback Devon Dampier (4) dances in celebration after scoring a touchdown during a game against Kansas at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News

item.title: Ex-Steelers OL Says Pittsburgh Was 'Exposed,' 'Embarrassed' in Loss to Bengals
item.description: Ex-Steelers OL Says Pittsburgh Was 'Exposed,' 'Embarrassed' in Loss to Bengals originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Steelers never had a chance against the Bengals on Sunday night, suffering a 38-18 defeat in an AFC North battle. Pittsburgh (6-3) is only one game behind Cincinnati (7-2) in the standings, but former Steelers offensive lineman Willie Colon believes that Mike McCarthy's squad was "exposed" in the blowout loss. "The blueprint is out, how to beat the hell out of the Pittsburgh Steelers," Colon said during Monday's episode of the "Bart and Willie Show" with former NFL linebacker Bart Scott. Colon, who won a Super Bowl with the Steelers in 2009, told Scott that Cincinnati attacked all of Pittsburgh's biggest flaws. Joe Burrow and the Bengals' offense put the Steelers in an early hole, and Pittsburgh was unable to match that level of firepower. "What you showed was, from the defense's standpoint, that if you win the line of scrimmage, take away their run game, neutralize their tight ends and force their wideouts to beat you, it's over," Colon said. "And that's what happened. ... This team isn't built to go toe-to-toe with anybody. This team is built to grind it out through four quarters, lean on their defense." Colon noted that Pittsburgh's pass rushers couldn't consistently put pressure on Burrow, who threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns. The Bengals finished with 484 yards of total offense (7.4 yards per play), while the Steelers produced just 222 total yards (3.8 yards per play). "We got exposed," Colon said. "We got embarrassed on primetime television." More Steelers Latest Steelers news How 'Renegade' became Steelers' pump-up song Complete history of Steelers championships

item.title: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
item.description: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword. Optimizely infrastructure delivers multipurpose malware Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript. Read full article Comments

item.title: BIG10 Secures 7 Berths in NCAA Men’s Soccer Tournament
item.description: The Washington Huskies celebrate after winning the 2025 NCAA Men's Soccer Championship in Cary, N.C. Getty The Big Ten Conference has placed seven teams in the NCAA Division I Men’s Soccer Championship led by defending national champion Washington and No. 1 seed Indiana. All first-round matches in the 48-team bracket will be held at campus sites Thursday. Three weeks of competition will conclude with the 68th NCAA Men’s College Cup on Dec. 11 and 14 in Cary, N.C. Joining the Huskies and Hoosiers in this year’s tournament field are Maryland, Rutgers, Michigan State, Wisconsin and UCLA. The Big Ten’s seven tourney teams are the most in conference history, topping the six which qualified two years ago. Defending champion Washington makes its 31st tournament appearance. The No. 5-seeded Huskies (10-4-5) play host to Cleveland State (9-6-4) Thursday at 10 p.m. (ET). Their quadrant is loaded with talent that includes top-seeded Indiana and No. 2 seed Maryland. Indiana (15-1-4) won both the Big Ten regular-season and tournament titles. The Hoosiers claim the No. 3 overall seed among the 48 teams, behind only Georgetown and SMU. Their lone loss this season came Oct. 16 at Rutgers, 1-0. Washington, Indiana Could Be Headed for Rematch IU is making its 51st NCAA Tournament appearance and drew a first-round bye. It’ll open play at home Sunday at 12 p.m. (ET) against the winner of Thursday’s Missouri State-Saint Louis match. If Washington and Indiana were to reach the third round, they would meet Nov. 28/29 in a rematch of last weekend’s Big Ten Tournament championship won by the Hoosiers, 3-2, in a penalty kick shootout. This is the 43rd tournament appearance for Maryland (12-5-1) and, like Indiana, the Terrapins drew a first-round bye. They’ll open Sunday at 1 p.m. (ET) by hosting the winner of the North Carolina State-College of Charleston match. Rutgers earned a No. 3 seed and will begin tournament play Sunday at 6 p.m. (ET) against either Cornell or Fairleigh Dickinson. The Scarlet Knights (9-6-3) are making their 19th tournament appearance in a quadrant that also includes No. 4 seed UCLA. Michigan State Gets Home Field for Opening Match The Bruins (9-4-5) are among the six Big Ten teams with first-round byes and will debut in the tournament Sunday at 7 p.m. (ET) at home against either Creighton or Omaha. They could potentially meet Rutgers in the quarterfinals Dec. 4/5. Michigan State (10-5-3), seeded No. 4 in its quadrant, returns to the tournament for the first time since 2018 and also enjoys a first-round bye. The Spartans kick off their title bid at home Sunday at 2 p.m. (ET) opposite either Marshall or Bowling Green. Wisconsin (10-3-4), also seeded No. 4 in its quadrant, is in the tournament for the first time since 2017 and will kick off Sunday at 3 p.m. (ET) in Madison against the winner of Thursday’s first-round match between Charlotte and Lehigh. All second-round matches will take place Sunday with the third round scheduled for Saturday and Sun

item.title: Mike Gesicki & Dalton Kincaid Headline NFL Week 11 Fantasy Football Tight End Starts
item.description: Nov 15, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki (88) and running back Chase Brown (30) celebrate a touchdown during the second quarter against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 11 cuts through the usual positional wasteland with a slate full of target monsters, mismatch nightmares, and defenses that flat-out refuse to cover the middle of the field. item.title: New York Yankees Dealt Good News on Top Free Agent Target
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 24: Brandon Lowe #5 of the Pittsburgh Pirates hits an RBI single in the first inning during the game against the St. Louis Cardinals at PNC Park on September 24, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin Berl/Getty Images) Getty PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 23: Brandon Lowe #5 of the Pittsburgh Pirates watches his hit go for a solo home run during the second inning against the St. Louis Cardinals at PNC Park on September 23, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) Getty Major League Baseball’s hot stove season is finally here, and it’s expected to heat up this week, with a number of roster deadlines on the horizon. The New York Yankees are expected to be as active as ever, and the organization got some good news on Tuesday (11/17) (MLB’s QO deadline) when 2B Brandon Lowe declined the Pirates’ Qualifying Offer, immediately making him a free agent. The Yankees are thought to have checked in on Lowe, as the power-hitting 2B is perhaps the biggest infielder on the market (along with Jazz Chisholm Jr.). More MLB on Heavy: New York Mets Quietly Trade 23-Year-Old Pitcher to Rangers Yankees Can Now Officially Pursue Brandon Lowe Getty PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA – SEPTEMBER 23: Brandon Lowe #5 of the Pittsburgh Pirates watches his hit go for a solo home run during the second inning against the St. Louis Cardinals at PNC Park on September 23, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) It was definitely expected that Brandon Lowe would decline the Qualifying Offer, especially after the 2026 campaign he had from an offensive perspective. CBSSports.com’s RotoWire staff wrote (about Lowe): “Lowe was acquired via trade from the Rays last winter and went on to slash .260/.331/.493 with 35 home runs, 96 RBI and a career-high plus-15 Outs Above Average at second base. The Pirates are interested in bringing Lowe back, but they will have stiff competition and Pittsburgh rarely wins a bidding war. If Lowe signs elsewhere for at least $50 million, the Pirates will receive a draft pick as compensation.” Lowe will likely sign for $50+ million. And with the Yankees not expected to bring back Chisholm Jr., Lowe stands out as an ideal infield free agent target for New York, but the Pirates will also be among the suitors across MLB in attempts to acquire his services for 2027 and beyond. More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Trade Idea Lands $70 Million All-Star Infielder to Replace Ha-Seong Kim Why Brandon Lowe is a Good Fit in New York While New York Yankees fans may say that the team needs to add more right-handed hitters, considering Brandon Lowe came off a 2026 season where he hit 35 home runs, there’s no telling how his left-handed stroke will play in the Bronx, which could only result in more longballs and extra-base hits. Plus, the Yankees are pretty familiar with Lowe’s ability from his time in the AL East with the Rays. Expect a lot of reports in the coming day

item.title: No. 8 UH cruises past Rutgers at Players Era 8 to stay unbeaten on season
item.description: UH's Arafan Diané (13) celebrates with teammates during the first half of Tuesday's win over Rutgers at the the Players Era 8 in Las Vegas. (Zach Del Bello via Players Era/Getty Images) LAS VEGAS - Dedan Thomas Jr. had 21 points, and the University of Houston jumped out to a big first-half lead to beat Rutgers 85-73 on Tuesday in the first game at the Players Era 8. Mercy Miller added 15 points, answering with a layup and free throw after the Scarlet Knights had cut a 21-point deficit to nine with about 13 minutes remaining. Rutgers (3-1) got within eight points, 69-61, on a spin move by Christian Gurdak with 6:17 left but couldn't get any closer. Chase McCarty added 12 points for the Cougars, who have won 44 straight regular-season games against unranked opponents. UH (4-0) advanced to Wednesday's 3:30 p.m. CT semifinals against the winner between No. 1 Florida and Notre Dame winner, who play later Tuesday afternoon. The Cougars played most of the second half without JoJo Tugler, who was in foul trouble and finished with four points and seven rebounds. The two teams were called for a combined 59 fouls during the game. Chendall Weaver added 11 points and six rebounds off the bench for the Cougars, who overcame two lengthy scoring droughts in the second half. Delrecco Gillespie had 11 points and six rebounds. item.title: Dolphins lose promising young defender to season-ending injury
item.description: David Brytus-Imagn Images. Dolphins lose promising young defender to season-ending injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As if the Miami Dolphins season couldn’t get any worse, Fins fans will now have to watch the second half of the 2026 season without one of their more promising players making weekly progress on the defensive side of the ball: Jordan Phillips . One of the more encouraging young players on the defensive side of the ball, Phillips will miss the remainder of the 2026 season after suffering a torn biceps in Week 10 against the Indianapolis Colts, according to ESPN Dolphins reporter Marcel Louis-Jacques. “Per source, Dolphins DT Jordan Phillips will miss the remainder of the season with torn biceps he suffered in the team’s loss to the Colts in Week 10,” Louis-Jacques wrote. “The 2025 fifth-round pick played 60% of the Dolphins’ defensive snaps this season and was poised for an ever larger role after the injury to Zach Sieler. A brutal update for Miami, which has now lost three defensive tackles to season-ending injuries in the past two weeks.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Initially drafted in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft out of Maryland, Phillips has found a home in Sean Duggan’s defense as an athletic nose tackle, amassing 28 tackles, 1 tackle for loss, and two QB hits over 327 defensive snaps . While it would have been interesting to see how Phillips continued to grow down the stretch in Year 2, especially with Sieler also injured , the collegiate Terrapin has proven he can be a legitimate defensive contributor at the NFL level and will be ready to go in 2027 when the Dolphins can hopefully take a step forward as a program. item.title: Magic End 1,429-Day TD Garden Winless Streak With Physical Play
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics got a wake-up call on Monday night. The Orlando Magic ended a winless run at TD Garden that lasted 1,429 days. This is not just a bad loss; it is a statement made by a team that refused to back down. The Magic took down the top-seeded Celtics with a final score of 115-105. That streak of losses inside the Garden has been broken after nearly four full calendar years. A Physical Statement The game did not start well for Boston. The Magic opened the night with a cold shooting start, making only 4 of 18 shots in the first 9:50. They managed just 12 points during that slow stretch. But the story changed quickly. The Orlando Magic made their final three shots of the quarter. They held Boston to just 17 points, the fewest the Celtics have scored in any quarter so far this season. Boston could not find a rhythm. In the opening half, the Celtics managed only a 34.6 percent shooting rate. They made only 7 of 27 shots from deep. Throughout most of the season, the Magic’s defense had not appeared as physical as it did. This shift in tone forced Boston into tough looks and low-percentage attempts. The Celtics’ six-game win streak ended because they could not handle the contact. Bitadze Makes His Mark Orlando found a key weapon in their frontcourt. Goga Bitadze served as a vertical spacer for the Magic in the second consecutive game. In 20 minutes of play, the 7-footer scored 10 points on 5-of-6 shooting. His efficiency was vital to the team’s success. Over the last two games, Bitadze is now 10-for-11 from the field. He has also grabbed 10 combined rebounds in that span. This win marks the Magic’s fourth-straight victory. It is easily their biggest win to date. The numbers show a team that has figured out how to win on the road. The Celtics must now deal with a Magic squad that plays with renewed confidence.

The Celtics’ six-game win streak ended because they could not handle the contact. Bitadze Makes His Mark Orlando found a key weapon in their frontcourt. Goga Bitadze served as a vertical spacer for the Magic in the second consecutive game. In 20 minutes of play, the 7-footer scored 10 points on 5-of-6 shooting. His efficiency was vital to the team’s success. Over the last two games, Bitadze is now 10-for-11 from the field. He has also grabbed 10 combined rebounds in that span. This win marks the Magic’s fourth-straight victory. It is easily their biggest win to date. The numbers show a team that has figured out how to win on the road. The Celtics must now deal with a Magic squad that plays with renewed confidence.

item.title: Arch Manning Leads Texas Past LSU Despite Three Interceptions
item.description: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Arch Manning threw three interceptions on Saturday night and still found a way to beat LSU 22-21 in Baton Rouge. This result keeps the Longhorns in the playoff hunt while knocking the Tigers out of the race. The win proves that a flawed team can still make a deep run if it gets the job done when the clock winds down. According to ESPN , Manning threw one touchdown on 19 completions out of 35 passes for 174 yards. Those numbers look bad on paper. Yet he made the one play that changed the game. He found Raleek Brown for a four-yard score with three seconds left. That strike secured the victory and cemented Texas’ place in the conversation for the next two weeks. The Manning Legacy Lives On Arch Manning grew up watching games at this very stadium. He pointed out his old seats to his teammates before the final drive. The win feels personal for a quarterback who has family ties to the venue. His grandfather Archie led comebacks at Tiger Stadium. Now Arch has joined that list of legends. “That’s what it’s all about: Death Valley at night, two-minute drive, let’s go,” Manning said. The quote captures the drama of the moment perfectly. He also called the win a memory he will keep for the rest of his life. It was a tough night for the defense, but the offense delivered when it mattered most. SEC Power Shifts Again The SEC might still get two first-round byes this year. Kentucky’s loss to Florida opens the door for other teams like Wake Forest, Iowa, or Oregon to move up. The conference could end up with only four teams in the top 12 on Tuesday night. Heather Dinich reported for ESPN that the committee is very high on Georgia. The Bulldogs dismantled Missouri on Saturday and jumped out to a 31-7 halftime lead. Their strong analytics and complete team play should keep them at the top. Meanwhile, Texas just needs to keep winning to stay in the mix. The Longhorns are not perfect, but they know how to close out games. Arch Manning threw three picks yet still led the final drive from the 42-yard line. He converted three third downs to set up the winning score. Texas now sits at 8-2. The team faces two more games before the final rankings drop.

item.title: Kelce Clears Ankle Scare, Backs Chiefs’ Snap Decision
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs secured a dominant 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, but the win brought a fresh worry for fans. Star tight end Travis Kelce left the field early with a limp after a hard tackle in the first quarter. He returned before halftime, yet his playing time dropped significantly for the rest of the game. Kelce addressed the situation after the final whistle, explaining that the team made the call to limit his snaps. Speaking to USA Today, Kelce said, according to Yahoo Sports , “I’m all good. I probably could have went more than I did when I came back, but it was the direction the team wanted to go, so I was right there with them.” He noted that younger players stepped up well, adding, “It was really nice” to see so many young guys step up. The 37-year-old had entered the game with existing ankle issues, a detail former NFL doctor David Chao highlighted. The Hit and The History The injury occurred just minutes into the game when Kelce caught a 23-yard pass from quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Video evidence shows Kelce heading straight to the locker room for his left ankle after the play. This moment felt different from a similar scare in Week 6 against the Chargers, where he played through the pain. Sunday looked messier, with fans furious over a tackle by Falcons defender DeMarcco Hellams that appeared to twist Kelce’s ankle awkwardly. Despite the pain, Kelce kept making history, having recently set the all-time record for career yards after the catch. While Kelce dealt with the injury, Mahomes put the team on his back with a massive performance. The quarterback finished with 348 passing yards and five touchdowns, his best statistical output in over four years. The Chiefs improved to a 7-2 record on the season, silencing doubts about their offense reaching previous highs. A Tough Road Ahead The team now faces a critical stretch of games with Kelce’s health in question. His fellow tight end, Jared Wiley, was also ruled out with a right ankle injury, leaving the roster thin. The Chiefs have a week to prepare for their next matchup. The team will host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET at Arrowhead Stadium. The offense loses its most trusted target if Kelce cannot go. Despite the scare, Kelce remains confident about his recovery. He told reporters that there were many questions about the team early in the season, but they have found answers. “There were a lot of questions, wasn’t there?” he said. “We got some answers.” The Chiefs beat the Falcons 35-13, but the win does not erase the worry about Kelce’s body handling the weekly grind at age 37.

item.title: iFixit’s Apple HomeView teardown reveals a device that will be difficult to repair
item.description: After finding recent versions of Apple's iPads and HomePods much easier to disassemble for battery replacements or other repairs, iFixit assumed it would be the same story for Apple's new HomeView hub that looks like a seven-inch tablet stuck to a smart speaker. The reality was much different and by the time they got the HomeView apart iFixit's skilled techs had "ripped a connector, snapped a speaker in two, and put more force on the poor logic board than any of us were comfortable with." The tablet section of the HomeView proved to be the bigger challenge to disassemble as a result of some questionable decisions with Apple's design. The … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Portugal’s new No 7 Forbs channels Ronaldo for winner as Wales are denied
item.description: One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese football federation put it. A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards. Turn a new page and all that. This was a welcome victory for Jorge Jesus, for whom a 4-1 home defeat to Denmark a few days ago was a harrowing juncture, and there were plenty of positive takeaways for Wales, too. David Brooks cancelled out Bruno Fernandes’s opener from the edge of the box and then seized the lead through Sorba Thomas, who applied the finishing touch to a purring team move. But Neto, who picked up two bookings in one minute and 59 seconds, the second for a foul on Brennan Johnson, equalised before half-time. Craig Bellamy’s side were fun and, at times, freewheeling but Forbs had the final say with a neat run and finish. Continue reading...

item.title: WHO sounds the alarm on antimicrobial resistance threat
item.description: The spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is threatening modern medicine despite progress in combating drug-resistant bacteria, senior World Health Organization officials said Monday. WHO officials said countries had expanded efforts to tackle AMR, but warned that progress in prevention, diagnosis and the appropriate use of antibiotics remained too slow to meet global targets. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Jean Pierre Nyemazi, Acting Director of the WHO's AMR Department.

item.title: NASA Launches Nuclear Power Systems Student Contest
item.description: The thematics for the 2026-2027 Radioisotope Power Systems Power to Explore Student Challenge Credit: NASA / David Lam NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write a short essay about a “superpower” of their own. Submissions are due March 1, 2027. Every mission requires a power source. Some of the most interesting locations to study on our Moon face some of the harshest conditions. Nuclear power could sustain human life and allow researchers to study the resource-rich environment despite freezing temperatures, long nights, and deep craters that never see sunlight. “As NASA returns to the Moon and establishes a lunar base where astronauts will live, work, and explore, we need to build an infrastructure to make it all possible. Nuclear power could enable exploration in the permanently shadowed regions near the Moon’s South Pole, carry robust science payloads over long distances, and keep instruments warm through the lunar night,” said Carl Sandifer, a program manager for NASA’s Space Reactors Division at the agency’s headquarters in Washington. “NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge prepares the next generation of explorers to use the unique power within themselves to dream up a nuclear-powered Moon base of their own design. We cannot wait to see what they come up with!” Entries include a 200-word essay and an original illustration. Essays should describe one of the students’ unique powers that will help the mission. Illustrations should convey the students’ vision of a nuclear-powered lunar base that supports human and robotic exploration of the Moon’s surface using both radioisotope and fission-based power solutions and demonstrate the students’ understanding of the kinds of exploration nuclear energy can enable. Judges will review entries in three grade-level categories: K-4, 5-8, and 9-12. One grand prize winner from each grade category will receive a trip for two to NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland to learn about the people and technologies that enable NASA missions. Every student who submits an entry will receive a digital certificate and an invitation to a virtual event with NASA experts where they’ll learn about what energizes the NASA workforce to advance NASA’s missions and sustain America’s leadership in space. Judges Needed NASA and Future Engineers are seeking volunteers to help judge the thousands of contest entries anticipated from around the country. U.S. residents older than 18 who are interested in volunteering approximately three hours should register to judge at the Future Engineers website . item.title: Nvidia: ‘I’d Be Honoured To Return,’ Jensen Huang On Possible Reinstatement
item.description: Former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has said he would be willing to return to the position if the company’s board of directors considers his reinstatement to be in its best interest. Huang made the announcement in a statement posted on his X account on Tuesday, his first public comments since stepping down on November 12, following revelations about alleged extramarital affairs and concerns over his personal conduct. The former chief executive said he had received an outpouring of support from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners and customers, with many urging him to return amid the company’s ongoing challenges. “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” he wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.” Huang, however, acknowledged that his personal conduct had fallen short of the standards expected of the company’s leadership and expressed regret over the difficulties his actions had created for the board. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” he said. “I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.” (FILES) Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia Corp., speaks during a news conference in Taipei on May 21, 2025. US tech giant Nvidia said on July 14 it will resume sales of its H20 artificial intelligence chips to China, after exports were halted due to US licensing curbs. (Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP) | I-Hwa Cheng / AFP His resignation followed reports of alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving an executive of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, which is under US criminal investigation over allegations that it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips in violation of American export controls. The allegations have also drawn attention to Nvidia’s role in the global artificial intelligence industry and concerns over the possible diversion of advanced US technology to China. The controversy has weighed on Nvidia’s shares, adding to uncertainty surrounding the company, which until recently was the world’s most valuable publicly traded company. Huang’s possible return has attracted support from prominent figures in the technology industry, including billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk and other artificial intelligence investors. An online petition calling for his reinstatement has reportedly attracted more than 190,000 signatures. US President Donald Trump also expressed support for Huang’s return on Monday. The Nvidia co-founder has been an adviser to the president on artificial intelli

US tech giant Nvidia said on July 14 it will resume sales of its H20 artificial intelligence chips to China, after exports were halted due to US licensing curbs. (Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP) | I-Hwa Cheng / AFP His resignation followed reports of alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving an executive of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, which is under US criminal investigation over allegations that it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips in violation of American export controls. The allegations have also drawn attention to Nvidia’s role in the global artificial intelligence industry and concerns over the possible diversion of advanced US technology to China. The controversy has weighed on Nvidia’s shares, adding to uncertainty surrounding the company, which until recently was the world’s most valuable publicly traded company. Huang’s possible return has attracted support from prominent figures in the technology industry, including billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk and other artificial intelligence investors. An online petition calling for his reinstatement has reportedly attracted more than 190,000 signatures. US President Donald Trump also expressed support for Huang’s return on Monday. The Nvidia co-founder has been an adviser to the president on artificial intelligence policy and is one of the technology industry’s most prominent advocates for the development of the technology. In his statement, Huang also reflected on his personal journey in the United States, saying he arrived in the country 53 years ago and regarded becoming an American citizen as one of the proudest moments of his life. He described Nvidia as his life’s work and said building the company alongside his colleagues had been a privilege. “NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honour. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA,” he wrote. He also expressed gratitude to those who had supported him and his family during the controversy. “To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours,” he added. Meanwhile, Huang is expected to appear before three committees of the US House of Representatives on December 1 to answer questions over concerns that Chinese companies may have gained access to advanced Nvidia chips despite Washington’s export restrictions. item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 launched second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?
item.description: null Voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference? On Nov. 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal — so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky. But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer? It comes down to choices made for speed and science during the twin missions' nearly 50-year journey, specifically during the first bit when they were flying by planets. The result is Voyager 1 is zooming out at a speed of 3.5 Earth-sun distances (astronomical units a year), while Voyager 2 has a more stately speed of 3.1 Earth-sun distances, according to NASA . Need for speed The original aim of both the spacecraft, which launched about two weeks apart in 1977 with Voyager 2 going first, was to look at Jupiter and Saturn. If funding persisted, which it did, the hope was to bring Voyager 2 past Uranus and Neptune, taking advantage of a rare planetary alignment. Voyager 1, by contrast, made a turn at Saturn to look at the planet's rings and the prebiotic (pre-life-chemistry) moon of Titan , before flying outside the plane of the solar system. NASA had a range of trajectory options to consider when launching the spacecraft, and elected to bring Voyager 1 at a faster trajectory — as illustrated in this video by Britannica, where you can quickly see the spacecraft overtaking Voyager 2 on its way to Jupiter even though Voyager 1. Voyager 1 arrived at Jupiter on March 5, 1979 while Voyager 2 got there four months later on July 9. The trajectories of Voyager 1 and 2 through the outer solar system. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Each of the spacecraft then performed a "gravity assist"—a sort of slingshot around the planet in which they took a tiny bit of momentum from Jupiter to gain speed as the spacecraft flew to Saturn. This technique is used constantly, such as recently when the ESCAPADE Mars mission flew two spacecraft by Earth on the way to the Red Planet, as it allows spacecraft to gain speed while saving on fuel. The planets themselves don't slow down that much. "Because the planet is so much more massive than the spacecraft, the transfer doesn't affect the planet to any measurable extent, but to the spacecraft it's a big deal," the Planetary Society wrote . "For example, we can calculate that during the Voyager encounters with Jupiter in 1979, Jupiter slowed down by roughly 10 to the -24th power kilometers per second — a change much too small to measure." item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Howell
item.content:encoded: null Voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference? On Nov. 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal — so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky. But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer? It comes down to choices made for speed and science during the twin missions' nearly 50-year journey, specifically during the first bit when they were flying by planets. The result is Voyager 1 is zooming out at a speed of 3.5 Earth-sun distances (astronomical units a year), while Voyager 2 has a more stately speed of 3.1 Earth-sun distances, according to NASA . Need for speed The original aim of both the spacecraft, which launched about two weeks apart in 1977 with Voyager 2 going first, was to look at Jupiter and Saturn. If funding persisted, which it did, the hope was to bring Voyager 2 past Uranus and Neptune, taking advantage of a rare planetary alignment. Voyager 1, by contrast, made a turn at Saturn to look at the planet's rings and the prebiotic (pre-life-chemistry) moon of Titan , before flying outside the plane of the solar system. NASA had a range of trajectory options to consider when launching the spacecraft, and elected to bring Voyager 1 at a faster trajectory — as illustrated in this video by Britannica, where you can quickly see the spacecraft overtaking Voyager 2 on its way to Jupiter even though Voyager 1. Voyager 1 arrived at Jupiter on March 5, 1979 while Voyager 2 got there four months later on July 9. The trajectories of Voyager 1 and 2 through the outer solar system. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Each of the spacecraft then performed a "gravity assist"—a sort of slingshot around the planet in which they took a tiny bit of momentum from Jupiter to gain speed as the spacecraft flew to Saturn. This technique is used constantly, such as recently when the ESCAPADE Mars mission flew two spacecraft by Earth on the way to the Red Planet, as it allows spacecraft to gain speed while saving on fuel. The planets themselves don't slow down that much. "Because the planet is so much more massive than the spacecraft, the transfer doesn't affect the planet to any measurable extent, but to the spacecraft it's a big deal," the Planetary Society wrote . "For example, we can calculate that during the Voyager encounters with Jupiter in 1979, Jupiter slowed down by roughly 10 to the -24th power kilometers per second — a change much too small to measure." "But each Voyager gained about 10 km/s [6.2 miles/s], a pretty big number," the society continued about the Jupiter encounter. This was "enough to put them on a fast path to Saturn — and in the case of Voyager 2, to Uranus and Neptune as well — and eventual escape from the solar system." Speeding on to Saturn, and beyond An image of Saturn captured by Voyager on Nov. 16, 1980 four days after the probe's closest approach to the planet, taken from a distance of 3,300,000 miles (5,300,000 kilometers). (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) With each flyby, the two spacecraft picked up speed with a single exception — during Voyager 2's encounter of Neptune. That's because the spacecraft made a turn to fly by Triton. The maneuver brought Voyager 2 over Neptune's north pole, before it turned and then was directed to begin "plunging down, out of the plane of the solar system," losing speed along the way. Voyager 2, in fact, did not have enough speed to leave the solar system until it flew by Jupiter. "It gained about 10 km/s at Jupiter, about 5 km/s at Saturn, about 2 km/s at Uranus, and lost about 2 km/s at Neptune," the Planetary Society wrote of the speeds, which are 6.21 miles/s, 3.11 miles/s, 1.24 miles/s and a loss of 1.24 miles/s, respectively. Voyager 2 images of Uranus in natural color, left, and false-color to highlight atmospheric features on an otherwise rather bland looking planet, taken from 5.7 million miles away (9.5 million kilometers). (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) At any rate, these fast speeds allowed both spacecraft not only to go fast, but to eventually reach interstellar space in 2012 (Voyager 1) and 2018 (Voyager 2), respectively. With the light-day milestone now reached by Voyager 1, it is anticipated the spacecraft could work into the 2030s, as long as their nuclear power sources can last. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, which manages the mission, has been carefully turning off instruments as required, and recently did a "Big Bang" procedure on both spacecraft to redistribute power supplies as best as possible. The idea is to maximize science return on both spacecraft, the only interstellar messengers we have, for as long as possible.

item.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records
item.description: 2 min read NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records Two NASA Space Apps Challenge participants in Vilhena, Brazil work together during the annual hackathon on their project submission. NASA On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% more registrants and was the 5th year in a row with increased participation. Since 2012, NASA Space Apps Challenge has hosted the two-day event, which has included more than 600,000 people from more than 190 countries. The challenge provides an opportunity for hands-on experience with NASA science, mobilizing an engaged global community of technologists and space science enthusiasts to answer questions that benefit humanity and drive exploration. Participants join events organized by local volunteers to work in teams and address one of the challenges and submit their project before the deadline. Projects are then judged to determine 10 global winners, to be announced in January. “The Space Apps Challenge invites people with many different skillsets to leverage NASA’s gold-standard datasets to address real challenges facing us here on Earth and in space,” said Amy Kaminski, engagement branch chief, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “We’re thrilled to see more than 180,000 people tackling these challenges and helping to accelerate our ability to find solutions.” One of the local winning teams from NASA Space Apps Challenge NYC pose with volunteer local lead Nate Cooper. NASA Challenges also feature data from 17 international space agency partners, all Artemis Accord signatories. This year’s space agency partners are: Angola National Space Programme Management Office (GGPEN), Bahrain Space Agency, Brazilian Space Agency (AEB), CSA (Canadian Space Agency), ESA (European Space Agency), ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), Italian Space Agency, JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency), KASA (Korea AeroSpace Administration), Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Center of the United Arab Emirates, National Space Activities Commission of Argentina (CONAE), Nigeria’s National Space Research and Development Agency, Paraguayan Space Agency, Senegalese Space Studies Agency, Spanish Space Agency, Turkish Space Agency, and UK Space Agency. Three agencies, GGPEN, AEB, and CONAE, also wrote challenges this year. To learn more about NASA’s Space Apps Challenge, visit: spaceappschallenge.org Karen Fox / Jessica Hall Headquarters, Washington karen.c.fox@nasa.gov / jessica.hall@nasa.gov Share Details Last Updated Nov 17, 2026 Related Terms Open Science Explore More 4 min read NASA Welcomes All Ages, Experience Levels for Space Apps Challenge Article 1 month ago 4 min read NASA’s Prithvi Becomes First AI Geos

item.title: Presidential Election: We Were Blindsided In Lagos In 2023 – Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works, Babatunde Raji Fashola, has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) was caught off guard by its defeat in Lagos during the 2023 presidential election. That outcome is one he says the party is “working tooth and nail” to avoid in 2027. Speaking in an interview on Politics Today, Fashola said the APC never anticipated losing Lagos, the political base of President Bola Tinubu, to the Labour Party candidate Peter Obi. “We were blindsided in Lagos,” Fashola said on Tuesday during an interview on Politics Today. FILE PHOTO: Former Minister of Works, Babatunde Fashola. The former governor, however, argued that the result reflected the growing maturity of Nigeria’s democracy rather than a collapse of the APC’s influence in Lagos. According to him, electoral victories and defeats are part of democratic competition, and political loyalties can shift over time depending on prevailing circumstances. Drawing a football analogy, Fashola said political parties, like football clubs, do not win every match and must constantly adapt to changing realities. “In an election, sometimes you can’t win everywhere. Most times, you can’t win everywhere,” he said. Fashola explained that in previous elections, the APC had strategically redirected its efforts to regions that were becoming more receptive to the party. He suggested that a similar approach would be adopted as the ruling party prepares for the next general election. “It remains to be seen whether, as happened in 2023, Lagos flipped, whether Lagos will flip back,” he said. “And we’re working tooth and nail to ensure that we take back what we lost.” Although he said the party was blindsided in the 2023 presidential election, Fashola dismissed suggestions that Tinubu had been politically “demystified” by the defeat, insisting that opponents underestimate the President at their own risk. He maintained that the APC remains focused on convincing voters that the reforms being implemented by the Tinubu administration deserve continuity beyond 2027. The former governor, who argued that President Tinubu deserves a second term, dismissed the ideas and plans being shared by opposition candidates. “What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform, growth, and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked. He also queried what he described as the opposition’s alternative message, asking, “What is the alternative message to what we are currently dealing with? What is the compelling message? Obi contested the 2023 presidential election, finishing third nationally behind APC candidate Tinubu and Atiku Abubakar under the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). However, he defeated Tinubu in Lagos State, where he secured 582,454 votes against the APC candidate’s 572,606. The APC has ruled the metropolitan state for 27 years. item.title: The MacBook Neo is receiving a rare $50 discount ahead of Black Friday
item.description: This thing is poised to eat their lunch. | Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge If you’re looking for a new laptop or a gift for the student in your life, you can save $50 on the MacBook Neo at several retailers, in both storage sizes and all four colors. The 256GB model is currently discounted to $649 ( Amazon , Best Buy , Target ), while the 512GB model with Touch ID is down to $749 ( Amazon , Best Buy , Target ). None of the retailers currently list an end date for the discount, which is the biggest price drop we’ve seen since Apple raised the laptop’s MSRP by $100 in July in response to the ongoing RAM crisis . MacBook Neo Where to Buy: $799 $749 at Amazon (512GB) $699 $649 at Best Buy (256GB) $699 $649 at Amazon (256GB) Apple’s budget-friendly MacBook leverages the A18 Pro processor, a chip originally found in the iPhone 16 Pro, to keep costs down. Both the 256GB and 512GB models feature 8GB of memory, and my colleague Antonio G. Di Benedetto was impressed by the vivid 13-inch screen and speakers, the latter of which are better than those in many cheap (and even midrange) Windows laptops. The Neo isn’t super performant, especially in terms of storage speed and total memory, but it’s great for everyday tasks, casual use, and students. Read our Apple MacBook Neo review .

item.title: Satya sorry for SaaS-y SNAFU - look over there, more AI!
item.description: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's Ignite conference keynote on Tuesday was all about trust. He opened by promising to earn back trust after last week's massive M365 outage and went on to focus on the need for organizations to trust their AI models. "So last week in some sense was really a reminder of how critical digital infrastructure is as the dial tone for the world," said Nadella. "We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. And in that context, I know we have work to do to provide that resilience that you can count on, the world can count on, and we are committed to ensuring that we learn and we continuously improve." Speaking at San Francisco's Moscone Center, Nadella described three areas of focus for the company as it works to build what he referred to as a frontier ecosystem: "Keeping the human at the center of it all, ensuring that you have ownership over your organization's intelligence and learning, and trust." Anthrocentrism is a tough sell just weeks after offering buyouts to 60,000 employees . Describing the shift from hand-written code to agent-written code, Nadella suggested developers have moved from building software artifacts to building software factories that build those artifacts. "The important thing here though is to remember still that that human intent, that judgment, that experience, skills, expertise all very much matter," he said. People may judge development work, but ask them whether they have the same sense of ownership as when they wrote every line. As to ensuring that organizations have ownership over their intelligence, that borders on heresy for a company with massive cloud computing commitments specifically to run AI workloads. If everyone really owned their machine learning models and ran them in their own data centers and on employee computers, Azure would be in trouble. Yet Nadella emphasized ownership – which isn't at all obvious given the legal ambiguity of who owns AI generated code and whether it can be copyrighted . "In the age of AI, the key question is how do individual firms continually build and own their learning and tacit knowledge?" he said. item.dc:creator: Thomas Claburn
item.content:encoded: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's Ignite conference keynote on Tuesday was all about trust. He opened by promising to earn back trust after last week's massive M365 outage and went on to focus on the need for organizations to trust their AI models. "So last week in some sense was really a reminder of how critical digital infrastructure is as the dial tone for the world," said Nadella. "We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. And in that context, I know we have work to do to provide that resilience that you can count on, the world can count on, and we are committed to ensuring that we learn and we continuously improve." Speaking at San Francisco's Moscone Center, Nadella described three areas of focus for the company as it works to build what he referred to as a frontier ecosystem: "Keeping the human at the center of it all, ensuring that you have ownership over your organization's intelligence and learning, and trust." Anthrocentrism is a tough sell just weeks after offering buyouts to 60,000 employees . Describing the shift from hand-written code to agent-written code, Nadella suggested developers have moved from building software artifacts to building software factories that build those artifacts. "The important thing here though is to remember still that that human intent, that judgment, that experience, skills, expertise all very much matter," he said. People may judge development work, but ask them whether they have the same sense of ownership as when they wrote every line. As to ensuring that organizations have ownership over their intelligence, that borders on heresy for a company with massive cloud computing commitments specifically to run AI workloads. If everyone really owned their machine learning models and ran them in their own data centers and on employee computers, Azure would be in trouble. Yet Nadella emphasized ownership – which isn't at all obvious given the legal ambiguity of who owns AI generated code and whether it can be copyrighted . "In the age of AI, the key question is how do individual firms continually build and own their learning and tacit knowledge?" he said. "For an economy to remain an economy where many firms exist and thrive, intelligence by definition needs to be broadly distributed versus just collapsed into a couple of models." Suffice to say that Nadella is promoting client control over AI data that's processed mostly on equipment rented from Microsoft, with some allowance for customer-controlled infrastructure. But that still ought to concern frontier AI labs like Anthropic and OpenAI that favor a white-glove, black-box service model where they are the arbiters of access. As for the third pillar of Nadella's vision, that's trust, which remains missing in action. "How can you even trust all this powerful technology?" Nadella asked. "And the reality is, by definition, you can't. In other words, it becomes an architectural imperative to separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it. And so our goal is to build a stack that addresses these three architectural imperatives." Microsoft's original stack was built on ownership of the operating system. But the company's commitment to AI is such that it now describes Copilot in the terms once reserved for Windows. "Copilot is the new operating system for work," said Nadella. AI is eating software, and Microsoft is here for it Fifteen years ago, venture capitalist Marc Andreessen famously observed that software is eating the world . Now AI, including Copilot, is eating software. "Apps are just plugins to Copilot," Nadella mused. "That's why we in fact have brought all of Office, all of its richness, right built into Copilot." Copilot is eating other companies too. Nadella said Microsoft is extending Copilot to take on specific roles by providing skills, connectors, and plugins for industry-specific tasks. Toward that end, " Copilot is the new front door to Dynamics 365 ," which now offers CRM plugins. And Nadella announced a partnership with Salesforce called Copilotforce that brings Salesforce context into Copilot, Teams, and Fabric. He also talked up Microsoft IQ , the company's new enterprise context management platform. "The idea behind IQ is to help every organization build, retain, and continuously improve your own intelligence across the organization," said Nadella, describing it as an externalization of the context system underlying Copilot. Nadella went on to announce a new model family for GitHub Copilot Fusion , its code hosting subsidiary's model orchestration and routing play. He noted that Copilot Fusion today is ranked above Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at less than half the cost on Terminal Bench , a measurement of how well AI agents complete tasks using a terminal. Then there's Copilot Workspaces, which Nadella described as a multiplayer version of Copilot. Instead of a chat window where one person interacts with a model, it's an interface for team collaboration that shares context with a model. Microsoft's decision model, intended to challenge TypeSafe AI's Jev, debuted about a month ago and now Decisions 1.1 is generally available. "We have improved performance, making decisions more accurate and responses faster," said Nadella. "Already over 4,000 customers have used it." He then said that Microsoft Foundry would offer OpenAI's GPT-6.2, which may have caused some confusion because at that point, OpenAI had no such model. A short time later, OpenAI announced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol. Microsoft also rolled out new coding models, in the form of Code 2, Code 2 Flash, and Cyber 2 Flash, and said its next-gen Cobalt 200 VMs are generally available. It's a question of trust After rattling off the various products and services Microsoft has prepared to help organizations with intelligence ownership, Nadella returned to the question of trust. "Today we can see almost everything that models touch, but you cannot see what happens inside a model," he said. "And really what's worse is that we know that what a model tells us about itself is not even independent evidence and therefore cannot be trusted. "And one model monitoring another model has the same issue. So you essentially have these unacceptable nested sets of black boxes, which we now need to make transparent and verifiable." Microsoft's bid to bridge the trust gap is the Microsoft Transparency Initiative . The company says this will involve engagement with the National Institute of Standards and Technology's "SI Agent Standards Initiative." Whether Microsoft AI will be compatible with NIST SI remains to be seen. That initiative also calls for collaboration with other organizations to develop accountable, verifiable, vendor-neutral AI transparency standards, and for Microsoft to incorporate this work into Microsoft AI, Foundry, and Copilot. Check in next year to see whether transparency is achieved. ®

item.title: ‘Even A Tomato Seller Knows Strait Of Hormuz’, Fashola Blames Global Conflicts For Economic Pressures
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has defended the economic policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, arguing that global developments, including the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and conflicts in the Middle East, have contributed to the cost-of-living challenges Nigerians are grappling with. Fashola, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, said Nigeria was not insulated from global economic pressures, particularly disruptions to supply chains, energy supplies and food markets. Speaking during an appearance on Politics Today, the former Minister of Works said the global economy was still recovering from the effects of the pandemic, which disrupted economic activity and production worldwide. He explained that shortages of goods following the pandemic had pushed up prices, while the Russia-Ukraine war further affected the supply of major energy and food commodities, including diesel and wheat. This aerial photograph shows boats anchored off Oman’s northern Musandam Peninsula near the Strait of Hormuz on June 27, 2026. (Photo by – / AFP Fashola also identified the ongoing conflict in the Middle East as another factor affecting global markets, particularly energy supplies and shipping costs. “It’s also important to contextualise the factors and the circumstances that have exacerbated the cost-of-living challenges,” he said. “Even the tomato seller knows the Strait of Hormuz and prices his or her goods according to replacement costs now.” ‘Helping Families In Need’ Fashola, a former Minister of Works, also backed President Tinubu for a second term, defending the administration’s response to challenges. Defending the Tinubu administration’s response to economic pressures, Fashola listed the minimum wage review, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), tax reforms, and the introduction of compressed natural gas (CNG) as part of measures intended to ease the burden on Nigerians. He said the minimum wage review was one of the government’s early responses to the rising cost of living, aimed at putting more money in workers’ hands. President Bola Tinubu during the inauguration of the APC PCC. However, he argued that increasing wages alone could not address the problem, warning that continuously injecting cash into the economy could create what he described as “hyper-demand inflation”. Fashola said the government had also sought to address some of the major expenses that reduce household disposable income, including rent, transportation, healthcare and children’s education. He identified NELFUND as one of the interventions aimed at easing financial pressure on families by supporting students’ education. “Your disposable income goes to rent, goes to transport, and goes to health care, and goes to your children’s education. And NELFUND was, okay, we will help families in need,” he said. item.title: US, Mexico and Bolivia lose measles-free status as deaths mount
item.description: The US has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus has spread at the fastest rate in more than 30 years, while Mexico and Bolivia also lost their measles-elimination status. Vaccination rates have been falling against a number of diseases, in the US and globally, and measles has been spreading throughout the Americas since 2024.

item.title: Atiku’s fuel subsidy reversal plan not realistic — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has challenged Atiku Abubakar to explain how he intends to fund his proposed return of fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027, describing the plan as unrealistic. Fashola said the former vice-president had not addressed the practical difficulties that could undermine the proposal, particularly Nigeria’s inability to fully meet its crude oil production targets and persistent security problems in oil-producing areas. He made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today . The former Minister of Works and Housing questioned the source of the crude oil needed to supply local refineries and support a subsidy arrangement, given the country’s production challenges. “If we have refineries working, what is our current oil quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because they are legacy issues, challenges with security people, vandalism. So where is this magic crude oil going to come from? People are entitled to ask,” he said. Fashola insisted that Atiku must demonstrate that the proposal can work rather than rely on promises to win public support. “If he can explain, good, let the people choose. But without proof, it is like abracadabra,” he said. He maintained that his criticism was directed at the policy and not the former vice-president personally. “The proposal is not realistic. I am looking at the proposal, not the personality,” he said. Fashola also questioned the consistency of Atiku’s position, noting that the former vice-president had supported subsidy removal during the 2023 presidential campaign. He said the change in position raised questions about the basis for the proposed reversal and what measures would make the policy sustainable. Fashola further argued that bringing back subsidy would involve legislative processes, as lawmakers would have to amend the existing legal framework to accommodate the policy. He wondered whether members of the National Assembly would be willing to support such a move, given its potential implications for public finances. The former governor also drew on his experience in the Buhari administration, saying subsidy payments had previously constrained the funds available to state governments. “I was in a government that was paying subsidy, and the states were not getting money. So are we going to go back to partial, near-zero returns, states borrowing money to pay salaries? Is that where you want us to go?” he asked. Atiku announced in August 2026 that he would restore fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027. He proposed a temporary, audited arrangement focused on petroleum products refined locally, arguing that it would help bring down fuel and transportation costs and ease the burden on households. Tinubu announced the removal of fuel subsidy during his inauguration on May 29, 2023, as part of his administration’s economic reforms. item.title: ‘Nothing Suggests To Me Tinubu Is Not Fit,’ Fashola Dismisses Health Concerns
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has dismissed concerns about President Bola Tinubu’s physical and mental fitness for office, saying he has seen nothing to suggest that the president is incapable of performing his duties. Fashola, a former Minister of Works and Housing, made the remarks on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he was asked whether he considered Tinubu physically fit to lead the country. “Nothing suggests to me that he’s not fit for it. Yes, he’s older. That doesn’t mean his mental capacity is gone. He’s still giving directives. And when I see him, he’s working. He’s still reading, authorising, minuting on things,” he said. President Bola Tinubu during his address to Nigerians for the 66th Independence Day anniversary on October 1, 2026. Questions about Tinubu’s health and physical condition have featured in public discussions since the 2023 presidential election campaign. During the campaign, concerns were raised by critics over his physical appearance, movements and stamina at public events. The debate continued after he assumed office in May 2023, with opposition figures and other critics occasionally questioning his capacity to discharge the responsibilities of the presidency. The concerns resurfaced in 2026 amid renewed scrutiny of his public appearances, including videos circulated online showing him moving cautiously at some events. The Presidency and the All Progressives Congress (APC) have repeatedly defended the president, maintaining that he is capable of carrying out his constitutional responsibilities. Tinubu has also dismissed speculation about his health. In September 2026, following an extended stay in Europe, he told reporters that he was ready to “work, walk and kick.” ‘More Mature’ The former governor, who worked closely with Tinubu during his eight-year administration in Lagos from 2007 to 2015, said the president had become more experienced over the years. Asked to compare the Tinubu he knew in the early 2000s with the president he knows today, Fashola said the president had become more mature. “Well, a much more mature one, certainly, without doubt. I am not the chief of staff he employed in 2002. That’s 39 years. I was 39 then. I’m 63 now. So we must give him that credit for the experience he has gained,” he said. ﻿ Fashola acknowledged that Tinubu might no longer maintain the same work routine he had in the past, particularly when it came to keeping late nights, but maintained that the president remained capable of handling demanding responsibilities. “Maybe not keeping late nights that he used to do. I’m not sure. He can still run the engine,” he added. When asked about opposition figures who have described Tinubu as feeble and frail, Fashola said such views were their opinions, insisting that the president’s actions and the activities of his administration should also be considered. I am not the chief of staff he employed in 2002. That’s 39 years. I was 39 then. I’m 63 now. So we must give him that credit for the experience he has gained,” he said. ﻿ Fashola acknowledged that Tinubu might no longer maintain the same work routine he had in the past, particularly when it came to keeping late nights, but maintained that the president remained capable of handling demanding responsibilities. “Maybe not keeping late nights that he used to do. I’m not sure. He can still run the engine,” he added. When asked about opposition figures who have described Tinubu as feeble and frail, Fashola said such views were their opinions, insisting that the president’s actions and the activities of his administration should also be considered. He argued that the president’s leadership had produced results in government, adding that Tinubu often moved ahead of those who underestimated him. “Every time he looks at you, you think there is nothing there. Before you know it, he has left you behind,” he said. Fashola’s remarks add to public responses by political allies who have defended the president against questions about his health and capacity to govern. The post ‘Nothing Suggests To Me Tinubu Is Not Fit,’ Fashola Dismisses Health Concerns appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Jensen Huang thrilled to be spending time with family, but will retake leadership burden if Nvidia asks
item.description: No surprises here. Ex-Nvidia boss Jensen Huang says that he'd be willing to come back to the company he founded, if the board wants him to return. In Huang’s first public comments since his resignation last week over a series of extramarital affairs, both with Nvidia staff and an alleged Chinese spy at one of its customers, he admits that he may have made life hard for the company he spent 33 years building, but he’s really sorry…and Nvidia couldearn really use him. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” Huang admitted. “I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.” But soft, what open letter through yonder news cycle break? It's one calling widely for Huang’s return – and he's happy to oblige if Nvidia’s post-Jensen crisis-mode leadership is willing to indulge him. “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said. “Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics.” Nvidia, Huang added, has been his life’s work, and is a “once-in-a-generation company” that perhaps needs his steady hand at the helm. There have been a number of public calls for Huang’s return to the head of the company he helped create, from tech industry heavyweights and Nvidia shareholders like Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, as well as a number of current Nvidia employees, company partners, and shareholders upset that the stock has lost more than a quarter of its value since reports of the affair first emerged. One petition pleading for his return has nearly 200,000 signatures . Faced with that, what else can a disgraced billionaire tech founder who may have literally have been in bed with a Chinese spy do? Duty calls. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang said. Reports citing Nvidia insiders with knowledge of the matter suggest the board isn’t considering reinstating Huang as CEO despite the public push. On the company's third-quarter earnings call late Tuesday, new board chairman Harvey Jones said that Huang's behavior was "Inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards and cultural norms” and that the board "does not expect to reinstate him as CEO," putting a seeming end to the question. item.dc:creator: Brandon Vigliarolo
item.content:encoded: No surprises here. Ex-Nvidia boss Jensen Huang says that he'd be willing to come back to the company he founded, if the board wants him to return. In Huang’s first public comments since his resignation last week over a series of extramarital affairs, both with Nvidia staff and an alleged Chinese spy at one of its customers, he admits that he may have made life hard for the company he spent 33 years building, but he’s really sorry…and Nvidia couldearn really use him. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” Huang admitted. “I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.” But soft, what open letter through yonder news cycle break? It's one calling widely for Huang’s return – and he's happy to oblige if Nvidia’s post-Jensen crisis-mode leadership is willing to indulge him. “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said. “Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics.” Nvidia, Huang added, has been his life’s work, and is a “once-in-a-generation company” that perhaps needs his steady hand at the helm. There have been a number of public calls for Huang’s return to the head of the company he helped create, from tech industry heavyweights and Nvidia shareholders like Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, as well as a number of current Nvidia employees, company partners, and shareholders upset that the stock has lost more than a quarter of its value since reports of the affair first emerged. One petition pleading for his return has nearly 200,000 signatures . Faced with that, what else can a disgraced billionaire tech founder who may have literally have been in bed with a Chinese spy do? Reports citing Nvidia insiders with knowledge of the matter suggest the board isn’t considering reinstating Huang as CEO despite the public push. On the company's third-quarter earnings call late Tuesday, new board chairman Harvey Jones said that Huang's behavior was "Inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards and cultural norms” and that the board "does not expect to reinstate him as CEO," putting a seeming end to the question. Huang out to dry The US Department of Justice made the rare point of commenting on one of the pillars of the Jensen Huang story on Tuesday when it confirmed that it’s investigating Megaspeed, the Singaporean company formerly helmed by Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen), the alleged Chinese spy. The DoJ has been checking the company out since 2024, when Alice Huang was still in charge, over potential export control violations. In other words, the DoJ is hinting that even if Alice Huang isn’t a spy, Megaspeed may have still been moving illegal chips. The DoJ added that Nvidia blacklisted Megaspeed in 2025, and that the Department of Commerce previously interviewed Alice Huang around the same time. It was immediately after that, the DoJ said, that it took over the investigation. “The Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security working together will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred,” the DoJ said. In other words, this is far from over and Nvidia might be justified in wanting not to touch its founder with a ten-foot pole. ®
