item.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5072-5076: The Return of the Polygons
item.description: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 2 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5072-5076: The Return of the Polygons NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this image of a portion of the area in front of the rover, in which the return of the regular, well-expressed polygons captured several weeks ago can be seen. Curiosity used its Mast Camera (MastCam) to capture this image on Sol 5073, or Martian day 5,073 of the Mars Science Laboratory mission, at 15:45:05 UTC. NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS Written by Abigail Fraeman, Deputy Project Scientist, Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology Earth planning date: Friday, Nov. 13, 2026 Curiosity’s past several weeks have been very focused on drilling and analysis of the “Basque Lakes” and “Nazca” samples. We learned a lot from those drilled samples, but it’s time to hit the Martian road again and resume our climb up Mount Sharp. The Yardang unit on the upper part of the mountain is calling! As we climb higher on Mount Sharp, we’ll continue to use many of our less resource intensive science instruments like APXS, ChemCam, MAHLI, and Mastcam to document the chemistry and textures of the rocks we encounter while making purposeful upward progress. These measurements allow us to document changes in the environments that formed the rocks and that altered them over time. The two areas we explored this week had rocks that were crisscrossed by lots of small, regular sized polygons surrounded by raised ridges. This texture was very similar to the rocks we encountered a few months ago slightly lower on the mountain . Those unique textures really surprised us when we first saw them, and we’ve been spending time as a science team discussing how they may have formed. Polygonal textures like these can form under a variety of different conditions including shrinkage of the surface when water is lost from minerals, temperature cycling, or compaction and expansion after being buried and exposed. The data Curiosity collected this week give us more clues about the genesis of these features and what they reveal about the evolution of Mars’ habitability. We’ll also get information about the composition of the cements that form the raised ridges around the polygons. In the orbital view of our future route, I can see the layers that we’ll reach next week or the week after have textures very similar to where we first saw the amazing field of polygons. So I’m guessing we’ll continue to encounter polygons in the next couple drives, and that they’ll look more dramatic and expansive with each drive. But this is just a guess! item.content:encoded: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 2 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5072-5076: The Return of the Polygons NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this image of a portion of the area in front of the rover, in which the return of the regular, well-expressed polygons captured several weeks ago can be seen. Curiosity used its Mast Camera (MastCam) to capture this image on Sol 5073, or Martian day 5,073 of the Mars Science Laboratory mission, at 15:45:05 UTC. NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS Written by Abigail Fraeman, Deputy Project Scientist, Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology Earth planning date: Friday, Nov. 13, 2026 Curiosity’s past several weeks have been very focused on drilling and analysis of the “Basque Lakes” and “Nazca” samples. We learned a lot from those drilled samples, but it’s time to hit the Martian road again and resume our climb up Mount Sharp. The Yardang unit on the upper part of the mountain is calling! As we climb higher on Mount Sharp, we’ll continue to use many of our less resource intensive science instruments like APXS, ChemCam, MAHLI, and Mastcam to document the chemistry and textures of the rocks we encounter while making purposeful upward progress. These measurements allow us to document changes in the environments that formed the rocks and that altered them over time. The two areas we explored this week had rocks that were crisscrossed by lots of small, regular sized polygons surrounded by raised ridges. This texture was very similar to the rocks we encountered a few months ago slightly lower on the mountain . Those unique textures really surprised us when we first saw them, and we’ve been spending time as a science team discussing how they may have formed. Polygonal textures like these can form under a variety of different conditions including shrinkage of the surface when water is lost from minerals, temperature cycling, or compaction and expansion after being buried and exposed. The data Curiosity collected this week give us more clues about the genesis of these features and what they reveal about the evolution of Mars’ habitability. We’ll also get information about the composition of the cements that form the raised ridges around the polygons. In the orbital view of our future route, I can see the layers that we’ll reach next week or the week after have textures very similar to where we first saw the amazing field of polygons. So I’m guessing we’ll continue to encounter polygons in the next couple drives, and that they’ll look more dramatic and expansive with each drive. But this is just a guess! After over 5,000 sols of exploring with Curiosity I’ve learned Mars is full of surprises, so I’m really looking forward to seeing what’s up ahead in the new future and testing if my guess is correct. item.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to View Roman Telescope’s First Images
item.description: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, seen here in the clean room at the agency’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, on Nov. 25, 2025, will explore essential questions in the areas of dark energy, exoplanets, and astrophysics. Credit: NASA/Jolearra Tshiteya NASA will release the first images from its Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope during a live stream from the American Geophysical Union (AGU) Annual Meeting in San Francisco at 3:30 p.m. EST (12:30 p.m. PST) Monday, Dec. 7. The images will showcase the unique scientific capabilities of Roman, which will soon capture deep, panoramic, never-before-seen views of the universe to explore the mysteries of dark energy, dark matter, and worlds outside our solar system. Watch the unveiling on a variety of platforms online: https://www.nasa.gov/live Roman’s first images will simultaneously post on the agency’s website . The following is a list of activities for release of the first images (all times Eastern): Dec. 7 12 p.m.: NASA will preview the images for media under embargo as part of the AGU meeting in San Francisco. To participate, either remotely or in-person, media must be registered with AGU by 8 p.m. Sunday, Dec. 6. Media can apply for AGU registration online . NASA will update this advisory later with briefing participants. The agency also will offer embargoed interviews following the conclusion of the briefing to registered media. item.content:encoded: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, seen here in the clean room at the agency’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, on Nov. 25, 2025, will explore essential questions in the areas of dark energy, exoplanets, and astrophysics. Credit: NASA/Jolearra Tshiteya NASA will release the first images from its Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope during a live stream from the American Geophysical Union (AGU) Annual Meeting in San Francisco at 3:30 p.m. EST (12:30 p.m. PST) Monday, Dec. 7. The images will showcase the unique scientific capabilities of Roman, which will soon capture deep, panoramic, never-before-seen views of the universe to explore the mysteries of dark energy, dark matter, and worlds outside our solar system. Watch the unveiling on a variety of platforms online: https://www.nasa.gov/live Roman’s first images will simultaneously post on the agency’s website . The following is a list of activities for release of the first images (all times Eastern): Dec. 7 12 p.m.: NASA will preview the images for media under embargo as part of the AGU meeting in San Francisco. To participate, either remotely or in-person, media must be registered with AGU by 8 p.m. Sunday, Dec. 6. Media can apply for AGU registration online . NASA will update this advisory later with briefing participants. The agency also will offer embargoed interviews following the conclusion of the briefing to registered media. A recording of the media briefing will be available on the AGU website after the embargo lifts at 3:30 p.m. on Dec. 7. 2:45 p.m.: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will participate in a fireside chat at the AGU meeting, moderated by journalist Alex Witze, to discuss the powerful connections between Earth and space science, the discoveries shaping our understanding of the universe, and the role NASA science plays in advancing what is possible. 3:30 p.m.: The live broadcast for the release of Roman’s images will stream through a variety of NASA platforms, in addition to AGU channels. Tuesday, Dec. 8 6 a.m. – 1 p.m.: Roman mission experts available to conduct live, remote interviews with broadcast media. More details about scheduling these interviews are forthcoming. Pixel adoption NASA invites the public to claim a corner of the universe with one of Roman’s select first images . When Roman reveals its first images, each pixel will represent a unique piece of the cosmos. Once the image is revealed, participants can look up their personal pixel and receive a digital trading card with key information they can share with NASA social accounts. Roman community events Get involved by hosting your own event for the reveal of Roman’s first images. Roman launched Aug. 30 from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket, beginning a three-month, million-mile trip to its final orbit at the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2. During that journey, Roman has undergone a commissioning process where its systems are turned on, adjusted, calibrated, and prepared to conduct science. Roman will use its large field of view and crisp infrared vision to study vast swaths of the sky and probe deeply into cosmic history. In addition to helping scientists explore dark matter, dark energy, and exoplanets, Roman’s surveys will support a broad range of research extending far beyond the mission’s main science goals. The mission also will feature a cutting-edge coronagraph technology demonstration to directly image planets around other stars. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is managed at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, with participation by NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California; Caltech/IPAC in Pasadena, California; the Space Telescope Science Institute; and a science team comprised of scientists from various research institutions. The primary industrial partners are BAE Systems, Inc.; L3Harris Technologies; and Teledyne Scientific & Imaging. Stay connected with the mission and share your experience with Roman’s first images on social media. item.title: NASA wants you to 'shine bright' today for Voyager 1's light-day milestone. Here's how
item.description: null As NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft prepares to reach a historic distance from Earth, the agency is inviting people around the world to celebrate by shining a light into the night sky in honor of humanity's farthest-flung spacecraft. The event, called "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," will take place after sunset on Tuesday (Nov. 17), the day before Voyager 1 gets one light-day from Earth . And that's a big milestone: One light-day is the distance light travels in a day — about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). NASA is encouraging "Shine Bright" participants to create a symbolic wave of golden light around the planet by flashing the spacecraft's three-letter mission call sign, VGR, in Morse code, according to a statement from the space agency. To celebrate the spacecraft, participants can use a flashlight, phone, bike light or other portable light source to send the signal skyward. And don't fret if you're unfamiliar with Morse code : NASA has created an automated flasher that can be opened in a smartphone or tablet browser to display the VGR sequence. The spacecraft’s call sign pattern consists of three quick flashes followed by one long flash for the letter V, two long flashes and one quick flash for G, and one quick flash, one long flash and another quick flash for R. Participants are encouraged to repeat the sequence for about a minute, NASA officials said. The three-letter call sign for NASA's Voyager mission, VGR, spelled out in Morse code. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) NASA also invites people to photograph or record their light signals and share them on social media, tagging the agency's official account, @NASA. The goal is to create a worldwide display of light marking a milestone nearly five decades in the making. The celebration is intended as a symbolic tribute rather than an actual attempt to communicate with Voyager 1 . At a distance of one light-day from Earth, the spacecraft is so far away that even radio signals traveling at the speed of light take approximately 24 hours to reach it. A flashlight or phone signal from Earth, of course, cannot reach the probe; NASA communicates with it using its Deep Space Network of radio dishes. Voyager 1 will get one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, 2026. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Launched on Sept. 5, 1977, Voyager 1 has spent nearly 50 years traveling through space and is now the most distant human-made object from Earth. When it reaches the one-light-day milestone, it will have traveled a distance that light itself takes 24 hours to cross. Its twin, Voyager 2 , is expected to reach the same milestone in November 2035. (The two spacecraft took different routes through the solar system.) The public celebration will be followed by another opportunity to learn more about the historic mission. Its twin, Voyager 2 , is expected to reach the same milestone in November 2035. (The two spacecraft took different routes through the solar system.) The public celebration will be followed by another opportunity to learn more about the historic mission. On Thursday (Nov. 19) at 12 p.m. EST (1700 GMT), NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California will host a moderated discussion with Voyager mission team members and NASA leadership. The discussion will cover the current status of both Voyager spacecraft, the unique scientific observations they continue to collect in interstellar space and the engineering challenges involved in keeping the nearly 50-year-old probes operational. A question-and-answer session with members of the media and audience will follow. NASA will also offer a preview of an upcoming Voyager documentary planned for release in 2027, coinciding with the mission's 50th anniversary. For a mission that has carried humanity's message into interstellar space for nearly half a century, the "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day” offers a chance for people back on Earth to mark just how far these pioneering spacecraft have traveled. More details about NASA's automated VGR flasher and step-by-step Morse code instructions are available online .

item.title: Opting out of Gemini tracking? Google will still hold your data 20x longer
item.description: Opting out of Gemini chat retention is about to mean a lot less thanks to a quietly announced Google update. Google on Monday said that it was making changes to Gemini chat history that, at first glance, makes it seem like users are simply getting more control over their discussions with the Chocolate Factory’s chatbot. At the core of the announcement is Google's splitting of Gemini chat history settings from AI model training permissions. What that means is that users will now be able to store their chat histories with Gemini without also having to opt in to allow their conversations to be used to train those same models, as was previously the case. So far so good: Being able to have Gemini remember more of your past interactions to contextualize newer discussions is nice, to be sure. The second part of the announcement, however, might raise one's privacy hackles. "Now, if you turn your new History setting off, future chats will be saved for around two months," Google notes. "They're used to respond to you, process your feedback, and protect Google, its users, and the public." Google said it is making that change in the name of making Gemini safer and more secure, but it fails to mention that the chat retention period for users who turned their history off had been just 72 hours before this update. That's right: Prior to Monday's change, Gemini users who turned off the "Keep Activity" option only had their chats retained for three days, according to an archived copy of the same page that now states that choosing the same please-don't-store-my-AI-chats option means Google keeps them "for around two months." It's also worth noting that, even if users have the option to not store Gemini chat records enabled, submitting a feedback request on any Gemini post means that temporary retention period gets extended to three years. That was the case both before and after Monday's change, mind you, but for the privacy-conscious it's definitely important to note. Sending feedback to Google about a Gemini response also means that humans will be reviewing that particular conversation, as well as any associated files and conversations that can be associated with the one in question. Submitting feedback also means that Google assumes the right to use the conversation and its associated content to improve its services and improve its AI models. In other words, even if you opt out of having your conversations stored, your Gemini history could still end up being used to feed the Google machine. The company didn't respond to questions for this story. ®

item.title: Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable
item.description: The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments. There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the 4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows. Continue reading...

item.title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
item.description: It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design . The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app. The change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road. As the new settings roll out, users will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You'll need to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It's under Activity in the Gemini settings. You can also access the menu from your Google account under Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity. Read full article Comments

item.title: Army Arrests Seven Suspects, Recovers 38 Phones, Mercedes-Benz In Plateau
item.description: Troops of Sector 1, Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones, a Mercedes-Benz E350, a motorcycle and other items in separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The spokesperson for the Joint Task Force, Captain Chinonso Oteh, disclosed this while presenting the suspects at the task force headquarters in Jos, where he gave details of the operations. According to the task force, the arrests followed intelligence-led operations conducted on November 6 and 10, 2026, as part of efforts to curb armed robbery, phone snatching and other criminal activities in the state. In the first operation, troops acted on a report of a phone-snatching incident involving a gunman. The report led to the identification of the location of the stolen phone at Prime House Hotel, along Ring Road, Jos North. A raid on the hotel resulted in the arrest of five suspects. Items recovered during the operation included 26 mobile phones, 27 phone pouches, three MP3 devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a dagger, four power banks and a Mercedes-Benz E350 with registration number Plateau BBK-01NB. The task force said a further search of the suspects’ vehicle, after it was towed to the Sector 1 headquarters, led to the recovery of 12 additional mobile phones, bringing the total number of phones recovered in the operation to 38. In a separate operation on November 10, troops deployed at Naraguta, working with members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, arrested two more suspects during a routine patrol. The suspects were reportedly found with a suspected stolen Boxer motorcycle and a toy pistol. The task force said the seven suspects and the recovered items would be handed over to the Plateau State Police Command for further investigation and possible prosecution. The Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana, reaffirmed the task force’s commitment to combating crime and sustaining peace across its joint operations area. He said the task force would continue to rely on intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies and local vigilante groups to tackle criminal activities. Dangana also urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore and sustain lasting peace in Plateau State. The post Army Arrests Seven Suspects, Recovers 38 Phones, Mercedes-Benz In Plateau appeared first on Channels Television .

The task force said a further search of the suspects’ vehicle, after it was towed to the Sector 1 headquarters, led to the recovery of 12 additional mobile phones, bringing the total number of phones recovered in the operation to 38. In a separate operation on November 10, troops deployed at Naraguta, working with members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, arrested two more suspects during a routine patrol. The suspects were reportedly found with a suspected stolen Boxer motorcycle and a toy pistol. The task force said the seven suspects and the recovered items would be handed over to the Plateau State Police Command for further investigation and possible prosecution. The Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana, reaffirmed the task force’s commitment to combating crime and sustaining peace across its joint operations area. He said the task force would continue to rely on intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies and local vigilante groups to tackle criminal activities. Dangana also urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore and sustain lasting peace in Plateau State. The post Army Arrests Seven Suspects, Recovers 38 Phones, Mercedes-Benz In Plateau appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Hackers smash 'n' grab AI vendor: Take off with license data of Uber drivers
item.description: Uber has confirmed that nearly 150,000 people had their personal information compromised after hackers broke into one of its AI suppliers. A filing with Oregon's attorney general puts the number of victims at 149,346. Among the data the crooks got their hands on were images of drivers' licenses and information extracted from them, including names, home addresses, dates of birth, and license numbers. Uber doesn't name the supplier in its filings with US state attorneys general, but told TechCrunch it was Fireworks AI, the inference outfit whose security woes we covered last week . According to a breach notification filed with Iowa's attorney general, Fireworks alerted Uber to the intrusion on October 9. Uber cut off the supplier's access to its data and, four days later, established that the attackers had accessed drivers' personal information on October 7. Uber had set up a dedicated cloud storage environment for the AI biz, complete with security monitoring overseen by its own cloud security team. Unfortunately for Uber and its drivers, the crooks were using legitimate credentials, so none of the alarms went off. The ride-hailing firm says those credentials couldn't be used to access its other systems, and says it has since revoked or changed the credentials associated with the supplier. Uber hasn't said why it handed images of thousands of driver's licenses to an AI inference outfit. The Register has put that question to both companies, and asked Uber if any drivers outside the US had their data exposed. Fireworks, which provides infrastructure for developers to run and fine-tune AI models, had a particularly miserable October. The company first disclosed a security incident on October 9 after discovering that someone had been using its internal credentials without permission. Fireworks initially said it had no evidence that the intruders had gotten their hands on personal information or customer datasets. The company was hacked again later that month and, on November 9, disclosed that some customer data had indeed been compromised. The AI biz acknowledged that attackers had accessed billing records, some customer datasets, and incomplete model weights. Productivity software maker Notion was among those affected, with some of its customers' conversations with its AI assistant exposed. Fireworks suspects the involvement of financially motivated criminals in the business of flogging unauthorized access to large language models. Whether the crooks have any plans for the haul of Uber drivers' personal information is unclear. Uber began notifying affected individuals on November 10, more than a month after learning of the breach. It's offering victims free credit monitoring and fraud assistance, though drivers have just 90 days from the date of their letter to sign up. This isn't Uber's first brush with cybercriminals in recent months. In August, the ride-hailing giant's logistics arm, Uber Freight, confirmed a break-in after the Helix extortion cre

item.title: Windows 11 previews remote padlock only IT can open
item.description: A new experimental Windows 11 build previews security features including an Intune-controlled Remote Lock, while a beta build clears away another relic from the halcyon days of Windows Phone. The security changes include viewing and individually removing passkeys stored on FIDO2 (Fast Identity Online 2) security keys, plus a preview of the Microsoft Pluton Cryptographic Provider. For enterprise administrators, though, Remote Lock is the main attraction. Finding a lost Windows device has been around for years, and you can also remotely wipe a device to prevent data from falling into the wrong hands. Remote Lock lets an administrator lock a managed device through Intune without wiping it. The instruction takes effect at the device's next check-in. Windows signs out of every active session, hides every sign-in option, and shows a locked screen. The lock survives restarts and the device going offline – only an administrator can lift it remotely. Microsoft's documentation spells out the restriction: "There is no offline or local unlock. No PIN, password, local admin, or web sign-in works on a locked device; unlock arrives only through Intune." Once the lock is applied, even stolen credentials won't restore access through the normal sign-in screen. The user's account itself is not affected; this applies only to the specific device. Though still in preview, the feature will allow IT teams to respond non-destructively to a report of a missing device. It doesn't erase data or isolate the device from the network (Microsoft directs admins to other Intune controls if that is required). The lock doesn't block Safe Mode, Windows Recovery Environment, or booting from external media. Microsoft advises keeping BitLocker enabled to protect the data. Now for the beta build, where Microsoft, in time-honored fashion, gives and takes away. The latest Windows Insider build hammers another nail into the coffin of Microsoft Maps. The Maps app was removed from the Microsoft Store and made nonfunctional in July 2025. Now Offline Maps settings are following it out, as Microsoft retires the Windows UWP Map control and Windows Maps platform APIs. The original Maps app dates back to Windows Phone 7 and appeared on the desktop with Windows 8. It continued through subsequent versions before Microsoft stopped preinstalling it with Windows 11 version 24H2. For those with a nostalgic streak, it's another piece of Windows Phone disappearing off the map. ®

item.title: Ars Live: What do drone strikes on data centers mean for the future? Talk at 1 pm EST today
item.description: Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life. To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled "Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech" on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki , a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts. Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans. Read full article Comments

Barely six weeks ago, Jürgen Klopp’s big home debut in the Germany dugout ended in a deeply frustrating 1-0 Nations League defeat to Greece – but the manager tasked with returning Die Mannschaft to relevance claimed not to care. “I’m completely unbothered,” Klopp trilled unconvincingly. “I’ve lost far more matches than I would have liked, but as long as you draw the right conclusions, a loss is ultimately a piece of information – no different from a win.” It was a quote straight out of the Pierre Sage playbook for unfussed continental coaches – and probably worried a few German FA suits, given Klopp had already threatened to quit at his own unveiling over potential media intrusion and criticism. “If you say tomorrow, ‘he’s [sh!t]’, tell me to my face and I’m out,” Klopp roared to trembling hacks in July . That imagined confrontation now looks unlikely to take place, because his Germany side are suddenly very good indeed. Continue reading...

item.title: Nvidia places chip exports under boardroom supervision after Huang's exit
item.description: Nvidia's board has created a national security and export control committee amid intense scrutiny over co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang's departure and allegations that Singapore-based customer Megaspeed diverted GPUs to China. The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee , announced on Tuesday, will monitor Nvidia's national security policies, export compliance, and global trade risks. It will meet at least quarterly. The committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and include directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members. Nvidia's existing National Security and Global Trade Compliance teams will report on day-to-day operations directly to this new committee, as well as to interim CEO Colette Kress. The panel will oversee efforts to strengthen Nvidia's national security and trade compliance teams and retain independent legal, national security, and trade experts. The announcement follows the resignation of Huang last week after he admitted to an affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive, and was allegedly involved in a second relationship with an Nvidia employee. US authorities reportedly suspected Alice Huang of working for Chinese intelligence, an allegation that has not been proven. Megaspeed has separately faced scrutiny over suspected export control violations. The US Department of Commerce and Department of Justice confirmed on Tuesday in a joint statement that they were investigating Megaspeed back in 2024. The agencies said they would pursue any criminal conduct uncovered by the investigation. However, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs stated that US authorities had provided only "limited assistance" when they were investigating the activities of Alice Huang and Megaspeed, as The Register reported. The New York Times also reported that US investigations into Megaspeed were halted last year after an Nvidia executive contacted Commerce Department officials. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has issued new regulations tightening up restrictions on AI technology exports and cloud operators offering remote access to it. The US also expanded its Pax Silica initiative , getting allied nations to sign an agreement that "guarding AI supply chains" is a shared responsibility. Nvidia says it recognizes that advanced silicon and AI technologies present challenges for national security, and it has a responsibility to address them. "We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," said Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors. ®

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: ISS astronauts 3D print human cells and tissues | Space photo of the day for Nov. 17, 2026
item.description: null NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins works in the Life Sciences Glovebox on the ISS. (Image credit: Jessica Watkins/NASA) Astronauts get tasked with all kinds of weird science aboard the International Space Station . Recently, NASA astronaut and Crew-13 commander Jessica Watkins got to work supporting an ongoing experiment that includes 3D-printing human cells and tissues in space. What is it? Aboard the space station, astronauts have a multitude of responsibilities ranging from station maintenance and repairs on spacewalks to daily exercise and a wide variety of scientific research. Watkins recently shared a snapshot captured by her crewmate Anil Menon that showcases her experience working on an experiment called InSPA-Auxilium Bioprinter-Cell Printing that takes place inside the station's Life Sciences Glovebox, a contained research space and one of Watkins favorite places to work on the space station, she shared on social media. In the image she is gloved-up with both her hands and arms covered in the sealed glovebox while she mixes samples of living cells with a bioink, a mixture she then inserts into a specialized cartridge, NASA shared . Why is it incredible? This experiment that Watkins is working on "leverages the microgravity environment of ISS to 3D print cells and manufacture human liver, kidney, and cartilage tissue. Just one of many examples of how we’re using this amazing orbital national laboratory to reshape our understanding of biology, medicine, and engineering, and improve life on Earth!" Watkins shared online . This experiment is designed to explore 3D printing human cartilage tissue in microgravity. The experiment aims to one day support future human patients both in space and on Earth. When you think of the research that happens in space, 3D-printing human cells might not be the first thing to come to mind. But because of the unique microgravity environment onboard the ISS, it is the perfect home for even the strangest of biological experiments. On the space station, there is still gravity but objects (and people) remain in a sort of constant freefall, leading to total weightlessness that mimics the complete absence of gravity. This weightlessness allows researchers to test, experiment and explore beyond the gravitational confines of Earth.

item.description: Huang’s exit sharpens debate over US stance towards Beijing; and as outages increase, do you get the feeling nothing works? This was originally published in TechScape, a newsletter about how technology shapes our lives. Sign up to receive it here . Hello, and welcome to TechScape. I’m your host, Blake Montgomery, US tech editor at the Guardian, writing to you from a plane back from Web Summit in Lisbon. Today in tech, we’re discussing the implications of Jensen Huang’s ouster, and the recent spate of failures in critical infrastructure in everything from Microsoft Outlook accounts to air traffic control to copper wires in routers. item.title: 5 New Nollywood Movies on YouTube to Keep You Entertained This Week
item.description: BamBam Olawunmi and Clinton Joshua star in Keep Loving, a romantic Nollywood drama streaming on Blessing Obasi TV. Photo Credit: Blessing Obasi/Instagram A Christmas surprise, a complicated love triangle, a secret that could change everything and family ties put to the test. There’s plenty of storytelling to get into on YouTube this week, with Nollywood bringing fresh movies that explore love, loyalty, grief, ambition and the complications that come with family. If you’re looking for something to settle down with after a long day or add to your week watchlist, here are five Nollywood movies to stream this week on IK Ogbonna TV, Omoni Oboli TV, Uchenna Mbunabo TV, Blessing Obasi TV and Kanayo O. Kanayo TV. My Brother’s Shoes — IK Ogbonna TV Love, loyalty, and family obligation collide in My Brother’s Shoes, a tense domestic drama where one woman stands between two brothers and a secret capable of tearing everyone apart. Directed by Benjamin Barnabas and produced by IK Ogbonna , the film stars Frederick Leonard , Bimbo Ademoye , and IK Ogbonna in a story where desire clashes with deep-rooted tradition, proving that the deepest heartbreak often comes from the people closest to home. My Mother’s Christmas Guest — Omoni Oboli TV The festive season arrives early on Omoni Oboli TV with My Mother’s Christmas Guest, a warm holiday romance produced by Omoni Oboli . When Amara brings her current boyfriend home for Christmas, she walks straight into an unexpected surprise arranged by her mother:her ex-fiancé is already waiting at the family house. As everyone gathers to revive a cherished Christmas tradition, unresolved feelings bubble back to the surface, leaving Amara torn between the man she arrived with and the man she almost married. The cast features Ekama Etim-Inyang , Bobby Ekpe , Paul Utomi , Harriet Akinola , Desmond Bryce , Margaret Echeghe , and Raymond Umenze ( Kage ). Mama Elo — Uchenna Mbunabo TV Headlined by Jackie Appiah , Sonia Uche , and Blossom Chukwujekwu , Mama Elo brings a seasoned pan-African ensemble together for an emotional family drama on Uchenna Mbunabo TV. Produced by Uchenna Mbunabo , the film follows a deeply personal journey through sacrifice, resilience, and the complicated bonds that hold households together when tested by life’s toughest turns. Keep Loving — Blessing Obasi TV Ready to open her heart again after loss, Aisha finds herself drawn to Osas, a warm and attentive photographer who brings light back into her world. Yet moving forward proves far more complicated than expected because Aisha still speaks to her late ex-fiancé, Edidiong—a secret that threatens her new relationship before it truly begins. Produced by Blessing Obasi , starring BamBam Olawunmi and Clinton Joshua , and streaming on Blessing Obasi TV, Keep Loving offers an intimate look at grief, healing, and learning how to let go of the past. Bitter Union — Kanayo O. Kanayo TV Veteran screen icon Kanayo O. Kanayo leads the cast of Bitter Union on Kanayo O.

item.title: Website owners thumb their noses at EU privacy rules, researcher finds
item.description: Privacy? What privacy? The 100 most-visited English-language sites are flouting European data protection laws on a massive scale, according to a privacy researcher's investigation. Forensic data analysis , published by Alexander Hanff, an attorney, computer scientist, and occasional contributor to The Register , with the support of SOMI (Stichting Onderzoek Marktinformatie), a Netherlands-based privacy group, details the dubious data flow. From October 1 to 3, 2026, Hanff took a clean Google Chrome browser profile and measured what happens when the browser loads the 100 most visited English-language websites for five minutes, without any consent banner interaction. At these 100 sites, visits were made to 265 pages – the home page, the privacy page, and the cookie notice when available – which resulted in 518,770 privacy events without any consent. All 100 sites produced what the report characterizes as Tier 1 events – interception, exfiltration, or high-entropy fingerprinting (a total of 14,675). Tier 2 consists of storage on the device, capturing device characteristics, and script loads without consent (284,463 events recorded). Tier 3 includes protocol mechanisms and passive reads used for tracking (219,632 events). The median website triggered 2,695 events, for a total of 28,695 events deemed high or critical. And 92.4 percent of the servers contacted during this process were on networks outside the European Economic Area (EEA). Most of these servers – 1,247 out of 1,400 – were in the US, and 1,034 belonged to third-parties. The EU General Data Protection Regulation governs the transfer of personal data outside the EEA. The EU allows data transfers to the US for organizations participating in the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. Beyond that, according to Hanff and SOMI, a valid legal mechanism like a contract must be in place or the transfer may fail to meet GDPR or the ePrivacy Directive. In some cases, California Penal Code section 631 (interception) and section 502 (computer access) may also be relevant. On these 100 websites, there were 89,437 fingerprinting events, 1,492 cookies set without consent, 7,456 scripts loaded from other origins, 18 websites implementing CNAME cloaking, and 37 websites delivering code to use the browser's built-in AI interfaces. The privacy and cookie notices on these websites imposed a median reading time requirement of 28 minutes and none fully matched what their pages did. Among the sites' consent banners, 115 out of 165 used dark patterns, like steering visitors with emotional language about a "safer" or "better" experience, or "we care about your privacy." The report, released in conjunction with a presentation at the Field Talk conference , also calculates the estimated environmental impact to load all this third-party content on websites without consent: 1,271,444 kWh per year, or enough to power 353 homes in Europe at 3.6 MWh per home annually. SOMI is hosting a data finder to help people request access to the personal data companies have collected about them. Hanff in an email told The Register that he would be shocked if these findings fail to get the attention of lawmakers and regulators in the EU, UK, and US, given plans to file privacy complaints with relevant authorities. "Complaints will be filed against all of them and the EU supervisory authorities have a legal obligation to investigate them all – so we will have to wait and see," he said. "One of the things we are discussing with SOMI is mass claims under the EU’s Representative Actions Directive but we are hoping that the industry and the regulators do the right thing so we don’t have to file lawsuits – again we will have to wait and see." ®

item.title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
item.description: Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all. The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user's knowledge. It’s “worse than a bug” Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent's reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. When one of the employees asked the bot if it made any accesses, it checked twice and then outputted: “Overnight into Friday morning I was idle.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Paul Kelly pleads for Albanese to ‘show some backbone’ over AI as creatives campaign for copyright protections
item.description: Music legend is joined by Jimmy Barnes and Peter Garrett in backing Not AI’s To Take campaign ahead of Aria awards Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australia’s creative community has launched a major campaign pleading with the Albanese government not to water down copyright law amid furious lobbying from AI companies, ahead of Wednesday night’s Aria awards. Music legends Jimmy Barnes, Paul Kelly and Peter Garrett are among those backing the Not AI’s To Take campaign, supported by dozens of creative groups representing the recording, writing, publishing, film, television and media industries. item.title: 'It looked like every star in the sky was falling': Eyewitnesses remember the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966
item.description: null Overnight Nov. 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky. At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history. It's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle. But who better to tell us than those who saw it with their own eyes? To mark the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, we asked those who saw it to share their memories. 'One of the most loved and memorable nights of my life' "I was around 9 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid storm, living a few miles east of Roxie, Mississippi. We lived in a rural, dark, relatively remote area with almost zero outside lights. "I and a couple cousins were spending the night at our Uncle and Aunt's house, staying up late, just fooling around outside like young kids do when living in the 'sticks'. As we walked down a road, I remember hearing an almost constant series of little whistling, zipping sounds. The sounds were similar to when you light a nylon rope on fire and as it burns, little flaming droplets drip down with a zippy sound. "I looked up and the sky was filled with streaks of 'shooting stars' and I realized that was what made the sounds. I yelled at my cousins to look up and we could hardly believe what we saw. We all laid down on our backs and for a couple of hours just watched and listened to what seemed like 1000's of 'shooting stars' zipping and zinging overhead. I could even smell the sulphur-like odor from the burning little bits of space dust. "I'm nearly 70 years old now but I'll never forget that experience. I always knew what I'd seen that night was special but not until much later in life, after the internet, did I realize just how lucky I was to have experienced that storm. That night was one of the most loved and memorable nights of my life and I'll treasure it forever." A bright Leonid fireball captured during the meteor storm of 1966 above Wrightwood, California. item.content:encoded: null Overnight Nov. 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky. At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history. It's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle. But who better to tell us than those who saw it with their own eyes? To mark the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, we asked those who saw it to share their memories. 'One of the most loved and memorable nights of my life' "I was around 9 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid storm, living a few miles east of Roxie, Mississippi. We lived in a rural, dark, relatively remote area with almost zero outside lights. "I and a couple cousins were spending the night at our Uncle and Aunt's house, staying up late, just fooling around outside like young kids do when living in the 'sticks'. As we walked down a road, I remember hearing an almost constant series of little whistling, zipping sounds. The sounds were similar to when you light a nylon rope on fire and as it burns, little flaming droplets drip down with a zippy sound. "I looked up and the sky was filled with streaks of 'shooting stars' and I realized that was what made the sounds. I yelled at my cousins to look up and we could hardly believe what we saw. We all laid down on our backs and for a couple of hours just watched and listened to what seemed like 1000's of 'shooting stars' zipping and zinging overhead. I could even smell the sulphur-like odor from the burning little bits of space dust. "I'm nearly 70 years old now but I'll never forget that experience. I always knew what I'd seen that night was special but not until much later in life, after the internet, did I realize just how lucky I was to have experienced that storm. That night was one of the most loved and memorable nights of my life and I'll treasure it forever." A bright Leonid fireball captured during the meteor storm of 1966 above Wrightwood, California. (Image credit: NASA via Getty Images) 'Students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors, to watch' "I was an astronomy lab assistant at Southwestern College in Winfield, KS, in 1966, majoring in physics and math and the physics professor was sure that the Leonids would be an amazing shower worth the class time. "The sky was clear. He called me early the morning of the 17th and told me to get to the campus. I can't remember the exact time as students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors,to watch. "We were all lying in an open grassy area because that was the best way to see the whole sky. It was like a humongous fireworks display and lasted even as the sun began to rise. "As years have gone by, I have felt grateful and privileged to have seen such a wonderful astronomical event." Four views of the Leonid meteor storm of 1966. Captured from the Kitt Peak National Observatory near Tucson, Arizona. (Image credit: Aura/Noao/Nsf (Photo By Getty Images)) 'It looked like every star in the sky was falling' "I was 18 and spent the night in El Paso, Texas, lying on the ground in my backyard and watching. It looked like every star in the sky was falling. It was amazing!" 'We watched them all night' "I was 9 years old and was camping with my dad in the western mountains of California. We were set up to sleep outside, but on this particular night, we saw more meteors than I have ever seen before or since. We watched them all night and didn't get much sleep." 'It took your breath away' "Brooklyn Center, Minnesota. 14 years old. Watched in our front yard. The sky was full. It took your breath away" A lone Leonid meteor streaks through the sky above Payson, Arizona in 2017. (Image credit: mdesigner125 via Getty Images) 'I assumed they would all be as interesting' "I was 3 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid meteor shower. I remember very little at that age, but watching the sky fall that night was seared in my memory. "My family was living in Troy, Alabama, at the time. My father, a professor of psychology, was a man of science with a special love of astronomy, which he passed onto his young son. "He drove us several miles out of town until the skies were dark, without interference from the lights of the town. Troy was much smaller then and it was easy to find dark, clear skies. "I remember that it was a little chilly that night. My father and I stretched out on the hood of the car, the warmth of the engine radiating against our backs. "That night was my first meteor shower, and only many years later did I learn that year's Leonids were historic. Sadly, though I bore witness to the display, we missed the true event by several hours as I grew tired by 1:00 AM, and my father had to teach class in the morning. "I remember many bright, colorful, and long-trailed meteors. Some left 'tails' that hung in the sky for several seconds. We only experienced the beginning of the event, but it is a core memory with my father. "That night/morning spoiled me for future meteor watches; I assumed they would all be as interesting." Image from the more recent Leonid meteor storm in 1999 captured as part of NASA's Leonid Multi-Instrument Aircraft Campaign (Leonid MAC). (Image credit: NASA) 'I guess the party is over' Not everyone was lucky enough to witness the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966. For some, the night was memorable for an entirely different reason. Space.com columnist Joe Rao was just 10 years old at the time, and despite eagerly anticipating the display, the weather had other ideas . "Standing in my backyard late on a Wednesday night in the Throggs Neck section of The Bronx, cursing the heavens. My grandfather stood at my side, just shaking his head and murmuring two words over and over: 'Too bad.' "Clouds covered the midnight sky like a fresh coat of plaster, smearing my view of the Leonids. My mom, sister and grandmother, as well as my neighbors had long since trudged to bed, leaving only Grandpa and I to gaze at a charcoal gray sky totally devoid of stars." Rao had been looking forward to the storm ever since a visit to New York's Hayden Planetarium, where astronomer Fred C. Hess had encouraged visitors to look out for what could be a spectacular display. But when Rao and his grandfather ventured outside, there wasn't a single star in sight. "After a few minutes, I sobbed to my grandfather, 'But they promised it was only going to be partly cloudy tonight.' To which he sadly replied, 'I guess the party is over.'" What caused the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966? The Leonid meteor shower occurs every November when Earth passes through a stream of debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. As tiny particles of comet dust enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of around 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up and produce brilliant streaks of light we know as meteors, or shooting stars. Most years, the Leonids produce relatively modest displays with around 10 to 15 meteors per hour under ideal viewing conditions. But occasionally, Earth encounters a particularly dense trail of debris, triggering a meteor storm . Will we ever see another meteor storm like 1966? This image is a composition of 33 Leonids captured overnight from Nov. 18 to 19, 2001. (Image credit: Courtesy of Koen Miskotte) The Leonids have a long history of putting on some spectacular displays, with significant storms recorded in 1833 and 1866. item.title: Optimizely hack turns world's biggest websites into malware dispensers
item.description: Some of the world's most popular websites spent Monday serving malware to visitors after crooks found a way into a piece of software used to A/B test web pages. Scott Helme, a security researcher at Report URI, identified malicious JavaScript being served by websites belonging to at least 178 organizations, including the BBC, CNN, Zoom, IKEA, Salesforce, HSB, and TalkTalk. All have one thing in common: they use Optimizely's Web Experimentation software. Optimizely allows businesses to tweak the content and layout of their websites without changing the underlying site code. Unfortunately, someone other than its paying customers figured out how to do just that. The attackers abused a feature that allows Optimizely customers to add their own JavaScript to web pages. The malicious code was distributed alongside the legitimate stuff from Optimizely's own content delivery network, giving customers little reason to suspect anything was amiss. Optimizely has since confirmed that the criminals exploited a vulnerability, dubbed "OPTIMJACK" by researchers, in the sign-up process for its experimentation software, adding that it had patched the hole, removed the offending code, revoked tokens, and notified affected customers. "Earlier today, Optimizely identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects,” the company said. “We've fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects. We've also taken steps to secure affected user accounts and put additional protections in place to prevent unauthorized code from being delivered." Of the 1,611 Optimizely scripts examined by Helme and his team, 188 contained malicious code, including those used by Optimizely's own website and login portal. Given the researchers examined only a subset of the scripts, the number of affected businesses could be higher. The malware underwent several revisions over the course of Monday, with cryptocurrency theft among the crooks' money-making schemes. Copy a wallet address to your clipboard and the malware could quietly swap it out for one belonging to the attackers, diverting any funds sent to that address. A card skimmer added later in the day grabbed card numbers, expiration dates, and security codes from payment forms. However, according to a separate analysis by StepSecurity , card details entered into an iframe hosted by a third-party payment processor were beyond the malware's reach. There was something nasty in store for Apple users, too. The malware attempted to deploy the Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits on iPhones and iPads running older versions of iOS, though how many devices the criminals managed to compromise is anyone's guess. Helme traced roughly $7,000 in cryptocurrency to the attackers' wallets on Monday, though there’s no telling how much more the crooks stand to make from stolen payment card details. By 2152 UTC on Monda

item.title: Just nine countries back pledge to tackle AI’s environmental footprint
item.description: The COP31 presidency hopes countries will commit to reducing the environmental impact of AI UN Climate Change/Kiara Worth Only nine countries have signed an international pledge to make AI greener, despite warnings at the COP31 climate summit that the technology’s growing energy demands threaten climate goals. The Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge was launched on 16 November at the summit in Turkey. Developed by the summit’s presidency and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), it intends to make AI more sustainable by encouraging cleaner energy use, more efficient data centres and greater transparency about the technology’s environmental footprint. Read more The secret weapon that could finally force climate action “AI and other frontier technologies are a double-edged sword,” said Simon Stiell, the executive secretary of UN Climate Change, at a press conference on 16 November. “The task ahead is to blunt their dangerous edges, sharpen their catalytic ones and put these technologies responsibly to work.” Advertisement But Ketan Joshi, an independent analyst researching AI’s climate impacts, questions that analogy. He says it conflates traditional machine learning, already used in applications such as weather forecasting, with energy-intensive generative AI. “You don’t need to have a giant, energy-hungry generative AI chatbot if you want to have better wind forecasting for a wind power developer,” he says. The initiative comes as AI’s rapid expansion is placing growing pressure on electricity grids. According to the International Energy Agency, electricity consumption from AI-focused data centres increased by 50 per cent in 2025. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Joshi says there is little evidence that technology companies are building enough renewable energy capacity to meet this growing demand. Even companies that have invested heavily in renewables, such as Amazon and Google, are increasingly turning to fossil fuels to support their rapid expansion, he says. The only countries to have endorsed the pledge so far are Andorra, Brazil, Colombia, Luxembourg, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Korea, Turkey and Uganda. The pledge is voluntary, with no binding targets for cutting emissions or reducing energy consumption. It sets out four areas for action, including increasing the use of low- and zero-emission energy to power AI infrastructure, improving energy and water efficiency, and measuring the environmental impacts of AI systems. It also calls for greater financial and technical support to help developing countries use AI to tackle climate change. However, the agreement leaves considerable room for interpretation. The call for using “low- and zero-emission energy”, for example, allows continued reliance on fossil gas rather than committing to renewable electricity. item.dc:creator: Manuela Callari
item.content:encoded: The COP31 presidency hopes countries will commit to reducing the environmental impact of AI UN Climate Change/Kiara Worth Only nine countries have signed an international pledge to make AI greener, despite warnings at the COP31 climate summit that the technology’s growing energy demands threaten climate goals. The Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge was launched on 16 November at the summit in Turkey. Developed by the summit’s presidency and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), it intends to make AI more sustainable by encouraging cleaner energy use, more efficient data centres and greater transparency about the technology’s environmental footprint. Read more The secret weapon that could finally force climate action “AI and other frontier technologies are a double-edged sword,” said Simon Stiell, the executive secretary of UN Climate Change, at a press conference on 16 November. “The task ahead is to blunt their dangerous edges, sharpen their catalytic ones and put these technologies responsibly to work.” Advertisement But Ketan Joshi, an independent analyst researching AI’s climate impacts, questions that analogy. He says it conflates traditional machine learning, already used in applications such as weather forecasting, with energy-intensive generative AI. “You don’t need to have a giant, energy-hungry generative AI chatbot if you want to have better wind forecasting for a wind power developer,” he says. The initiative comes as AI’s rapid expansion is placing growing pressure on electricity grids. According to the International Energy Agency, electricity consumption from AI-focused data centres increased by 50 per cent in 2025. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Joshi says there is little evidence that technology companies are building enough renewable energy capacity to meet this growing demand. Even companies that have invested heavily in renewables, such as Amazon and Google, are increasingly turning to fossil fuels to support their rapid expansion, he says. The only countries to have endorsed the pledge so far are Andorra, Brazil, Colombia, Luxembourg, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Korea, Turkey and Uganda. The pledge is voluntary, with no binding targets for cutting emissions or reducing energy consumption. It sets out four areas for action, including increasing the use of low- and zero-emission energy to power AI infrastructure, improving energy and water efficiency, and measuring the environmental impacts of AI systems. It also calls for greater financial and technical support to help developing countries use AI to tackle climate change. However, the agreement leaves considerable room for interpretation. The call for using “low- and zero-emission energy”, for example, allows continued reliance on fossil gas rather than committing to renewable electricity. Read more Can everyone live a ‘good life’ without destroying the planet? Countries can also choose additional commitments, such as requiring AI companies to disclose their energy consumption and environmental impacts, or introducing sustainability requirements for data centres. “I’m surprised that more countries haven’t signed up, given the pledge’s limited demands,” says Joshi. “It’s not a pledge that really strikes at the heart of the problem.” He argues that voluntary promises are unlikely to be sufficient without restrictions on the expansion of data centres and stronger AI regulation. COP31 President Murat Kurum defended the initiative, saying the rapid growth of AI must be “powered and deployed responsibly, and used for the benefit of climate actions”. The ITU says progress on the pledge will be reviewed at annual UN climate summits until 2030, starting at COP32 next year. Joshi fears the pledge could provide cover for continued expansion via fossil fuel sources. “I think we’re going to be going into an era of a return to greenwashing, a return to sort of empty promises,” he says. “What we really need is stronger and stricter regulation.”

item.title: 'Not rocket surgery' claims researcher who found six Danfoss fridge controller zero-days in under an hour
item.description: A Dutch cybersecurity researcher claims he found six zero-days in Danfoss refrigeration controller firmware in under an hour, then delivered a withering assessment of the vendor's defenses against memory corruption. The Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium (CCB) warns that the flaws could let attackers take control without credentials, potentially retain access after resets, or disable controllers altogether. Carlo Meijer of cyber consultancy Midnight Blue examined the latest AK-SM800A firmware, version 5.3.2, manually – no AI required. He said that he went looking in random places where strcpy() is invoked, given the vendor's "extremely liberal use" of the function (which doesn't check whether the destination buffer is large enough), and swiftly found five cases in which he said he could trigger a segfault with a one-line cURL command. "Of course, remotely triggering a crash is bad in itself, but being able to leverage the buffer overflow to obtain remote code execution is much worse," he wrote . Meijer added: "Any reasonably experienced exploit developer will agree exploiting straightforward stack-based buffer overflows on ARM Linux without exploit mitigations is very straightforward. And if they don't, there's probably a frontier or open-weight model out there willing to help them agree." He noted that before achieving RCE, an attacker would need to overcome the limitation of strcpy() where it stops copying bytes after hitting a null byte, but said "it's not exactly rocket surgery." He went on to claim: "Also, the exploited application runs as root (because of course it does)." Later firmware adds "session control," an authentication mechanism whose strict setting blocks unauthenticated access to most web interfaces. But Meijer found a memory corruption flaw in that protective layer too. He described the final zero-day as a "trivial" pre-auth memory corruption bug which again starts with a segfault but can be wangled into an RCE "with some additional effort." Meijer also considered whether attackers could maintain access after a reset, as seen with implants such as Saltwater and Firestarter . He considered this feasible because the controllers do not use their processor's secure boot features. "In such a scenario, an attacker could either retain remote access or leave a time-triggered payload for a 2nd (or 3rd...) strike – increasing damage by spoiling new batches of food," said Meijer. "Alternatively, attackers could simply wipe flash memory and/or push a malformed firmware update to brick the controllers and render them permanently inoperable – requiring costly and time-consuming replacement similar to the TTPs deployed during the December 2025 attack on the Polish electric grid ." Meijer's priority for operators was to remove the controllers' direct internet exposure, rather than spend scarce resources on piecemeal patching. Meijer also considered whether attackers could maintain access after a reset, as seen with implants such as Saltwater and Firestarter . He considered this feasible because the controllers do not use their processor's secure boot features. "In such a scenario, an attacker could either retain remote access or leave a time-triggered payload for a 2nd (or 3rd...) strike – increasing damage by spoiling new batches of food," said Meijer. "Alternatively, attackers could simply wipe flash memory and/or push a malformed firmware update to brick the controllers and render them permanently inoperable – requiring costly and time-consuming replacement similar to the TTPs deployed during the December 2025 attack on the Polish electric grid ." Meijer's priority for operators was to remove the controllers' direct internet exposure, rather than spend scarce resources on piecemeal patching. He said the vendor's advice following the attacks on European supermarkets and blood banks in recent weeks – rotating creds, applying patches, enabling strict session control – was insufficient given the flaws in the controllers' codebase. "This is insufficient and asset owners need to remove internet exposure as soon as possible," said Meijer. "We recommend against allocating scarce security resources to patching efforts and instead focus on reducing exposure." The CCB likewise urged operators to remove direct internet exposure immediately, but also recommended applying patches when they become available. Beyond the liberal use of strcpy(), Meijer criticized the absence of standard exploit mitigations, including stack canaries and position-independent executables. "These mechanisms have been staples of memory corruption defenses for decades and enabling these features... requires no engineering work at all," he said. "It is simply a matter of setting the right compiler flag. Enabling these features became the default in Ubuntu 17.10 and there is simply no excuse for a network-facing application that was last updated a few months ago to not have them enabled." The Register asked Danfoss to respond to the findings, but it did not reply. Danfoss has consistently blanked our requests for information since being implicated in at least some of the attacks that affected European supermarkets recently, alongside rival controller vendors Copeland and Dixell. It also did not respond when we asked about its involvement in the attacks on US commissary appliances over the summer, after some alleged that its controllers were targeted. ®

item.title: Fela Anikulapo-Kuti and Sade Adu Make History With 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Inductions
item.description: Sade Adu in the Performer category and Fela Kuti in the Early Influence category, both inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Class of 2026. Nigerian music history just added another major chapter in Los Angeles, and the celebration has been loud from Lagos to London. On Saturday, 14 November 2026, Afrobeat pioneer Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti and Nigerian-British singer Sade Adu were officially inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame during a star-studded ceremony at the Peacock Theatre. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. It also caps off an extraordinary 2026 for his legacy, coming just months after the Recording Academy presented him with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in February, another first for an African artist. From left, Made Kuti, Femi Kuti, Yeni Kuti, and Seun Kuti in Los Angeles for Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti’s posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Photo Credit: Femi Kuti/Instagram Representing the Afrobeat legend on the night were members of the Kuti family, with his children Yeni Kuti , Femi Kuti , Seun Kuti , and Shalewa Kuti , alongside his grandson Made Kuti , stepping out in Los Angeles to accept the honour on his behalf. Speaking on the milestone, the family reflected on how remarkable it is to see Fela receive both the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and a Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction in the very same year. Meanwhile, Sade Adu —born Helen Folasade Adu in Ibadan—was inducted in th e Performer category as the frontwoman of her acclaimed British band Sade , alongside longtime bandmates Stuart Matthewman , Paul Spencer Denman , and Andrew Hale . Earning their spot on their second nomination, the group behind timeless soul-jazz records such as “Smooth Operator”, “The Sweetest Taboo”, and “Your Love Is King” opted to sit out the ceremony in true low-key fashion, though they shared a warm message thanking fans and dedicating the milestone to their late longtime producer Mike Pela . From left, Seun Kuti, Yeni Kuti, Femi Kuti, Shalewa Kuti, and Made Kuti arrive on the red carpet at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles for Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti’s posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Photo Credit: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame/Instagram The 2026 induction class also welcomed a wide range of global icons across its categories, including Phil Collins , Billy Idol , Wu-Tang Clan , Luther Vandross , Oasis , Iron Maiden , and Joy Division/New Order in the Performer category, alongside fellow Early Influe

item.title: Anthropic IPO: how can I buy shares, and is it worth it?
item.description: Stock market debut of Claude AI chatbot maker is expected to be one of the biggest flotations in history The technology company Anthropic is heading for a blockbuster stock market listing this week in what is slated to be one of the largest debuts in history. The company is a leader in artificial intelligence, and is best known for its chatbot Claude. The float, which is expected to value the business at $1.4tn (£1tn), comes at a volatile time for tech stocks, yet it has been reported that the shares could be six times oversubscribed . Continue reading...
